def normalize_category(value: str, fallback: str = "") -> str:
    """Map source collection/table names to challenge policy categories."""
    candidate = value.strip().upper().replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "_")
    if candidate in CATEGORY_ALIASES:
        return CATEGORY_ALIASES[candidate]
    lowered = f"{candidate} {fallback.upper()}"
    if "TOMBSTONE" in lowered or "DELETED_CUSTOMER_REFERENCE" in lowered:
        return "ACCOUNT_TOMBSTONE"
    if "SECURITY" in lowered or "AUDIT_RECORD" in lowered or "AUDIT_EVENT" in lowered:
        return "SECURITY_AUDIT_LOG"
    if "LEGAL_HOLD" in lowered or "RETAINED_ORDER" in lowered:
        return "LEGAL_HOLD_RECORD"
    if "BACKUP" in lowered or "RESTORE" in lowered or "ARCHIVE" in lowered:
        return "BACKUP_ARCHIVE"
    if "CONNECTOR" in lowered or "DATA_FLOW" in lowered or "SUBSCRIPTION" in lowered:
        return "DATA_FLOW"
    if "IMPORT_PIPELINE" in lowered or "SYNC_PIPELINE" in lowered or "DATA_IMPORT" in lowered:
        return "DATA_FLOW"
    if "SEARCH" in lowered or "INDEX" in lowered:
        return "SEARCH_INDEX_ENTRY"
    if "CACHE" in lowered:
        return "CACHE_ENTRY"
    if "ANALYTIC" in lowered:
        return "ANALYTICS_PROFILE"
    if "TELEMETRY" in lowered or "PRODUCT_EVENT" in lowered:
        return "PRODUCT_TELEMETRY"
    if "EXPORT" in lowered:
        return "USER_EXPORT"
    if "MARKETING" in lowered:
        return "MARKETING_PROFILE"
    if "DELIVERY" in lowered or "EMAIL_LOG" in lowered:
        return "EMAIL_DELIVERY_LOG"
    if "ATTACHMENT" in lowered:
        return "SUPPORT_ATTACHMENT"
    if "SUPPORT" in lowered or "TICKET" in lowered or "CONVERSATION" in lowered:
        return "SUPPORT_MESSAGE"
    if "PROFILE" in lowered or "ACCOUNT_PROFILE" in lowered or "ACCOUNT_SERVICE" in lowered:
        return "USER_PROFILE"
    if re.search(r"\baccount[_-]\d+\b", lowered):
        return "USER_PROFILE"
    if "SECONDARY_IDENTIFIER" in lowered:
        return "SECONDARY_IDENTIFIER"
    return ""


def infer_system(value: str, category: str = "", component: str = "") -> str:
    candidate = " ".join((value, component)).casefold()
    if "identity" in candidate or "tombstone" in candidate:
        return "identity_service"
    if "account" in candidate or category == "USER_PROFILE":
        return "account_service"
    if "search" in candidate or category == "SEARCH_INDEX_ENTRY":
        return "search_service"
    if "analytics" in candidate or category == "ANALYTICS_PROFILE":
        return "analytics_platform"
    if "support" in candidate or category in {"SUPPORT_MESSAGE", "SUPPORT_ATTACHMENT"}:
        return "support_platform"
    if "security" in candidate or category == "SECURITY_AUDIT_LOG":
        return "security_service"
    if "legal" in candidate or category == "LEGAL_HOLD_RECORD":
        return "legal_service"
    if "backup" in candidate or "restore" in candidate or category == "BACKUP_ARCHIVE":
        return "backup_service"
    if "connector" in candidate or "integration" in candidate or category == "DATA_FLOW":
        return "integration_service"
    if "export" in candidate or category == "USER_EXPORT":
        return "export_service"
    if "marketing" in candidate or category == "MARKETING_PROFILE":
        return "marketing_service"
    if "delivery" in candidate or category == "EMAIL_DELIVERY_LOG":
        return "email_delivery_service"
    if "cache" in candidate or category == "CACHE_ENTRY":
        return "cache_service"
    if "telemetry" in candidate or category == "PRODUCT_TELEMETRY":
        return "telemetry_service"
    return value.strip() or "unknown_system"


def _first_text(fields: Mapping[str, Any], keys: Iterable[str]) -> str:
    for key in keys:
        value = fields.get(key)
        if isinstance(value, (str, int, float)) and str(value).strip():
            return str(value).strip()
    return ""


def _flatten_text(value: Any) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
        return " ".join(f"{key} {_flatten_text(item)}" for key, item in value.items())
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, set)):
        return " ".join(_flatten_text(item) for item in value)
    return str(value) if value is not None else ""


def _resource_id(fields: Mapping[str, Any], text: str = "") -> str:
    value = _first_text(fields, ("resource_id", "_id", "record_id", "tombstone_id", "ticket_id", "archive_id", "export_id", "object_id"))
    if value:
        return value
    match = RESOURCE_PATTERN.search(text)
    return match.group(0) if match else ""


def _make_record(
    evidence_id: str,
    available_at: str,
    file_path: str,
    source_kind: str,
    fields: Mapping[str, Any],
    context: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    text: str = "",
    observed_at: str = "",
    resource_override: str = "",
) -> EvidenceRecord:
    context = context or {}
    combined = {**context, **fields}
    category_value = _first_text(combined, ("data_category", "record_type", "category", "collection", "table_name"))
    category = normalize_category(
        category_value,
        " ".join((file_path, context.get("service", ""), context.get("data_store", ""), context.get("origin_system", ""))),
    )
    component = _first_text(combined, ("collection", "table_name", "source_component", "system")) or context.get("collection", "") or context.get("table", "")
    system_value = _first_text(combined, ("system_id", "system", "service", "service_id", "origin_system", "data_store", "source_system"))
    system_id = infer_system(system_value or context.get("service", "") or context.get("data_store", "") or context.get("origin", ""), category, component)
    timestamp = observed_at or _first_text(combined, ("observed_at", "recorded_at", "event_time", "captured_at", "updated_at", "indexed_at", "created_at", "exported_at")) or available_at
    rendered = text or _flatten_text(fields)
    return EvidenceRecord(
        evidence_id=evidence_id,
        available_at=available_at,
        observed_at=timestamp,
        system_id=system_id,
        resource_id=resource_override or _resource_id(fields, rendered),
        data_category=category,
        source_component=component or source_kind,
        file_path=file_path,
        source_kind=source_kind,
        fields=dict(fields),
        text=rendered,
    )


def _looks_like_record(value: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    return any(key in value for key in ("resource_id", "_id", "record_id", "tombstone_id", "ticket_id", "archive_id", "export_id", "object_id"))

    def walk(value: Any, context: dict[str, str], parent_key: str = "") -> None:
        if isinstance(value, list):

        if not isinstance(value, Mapping):

        for key in ("source", "origin", "service", "system", "system_id", "origin_system", "data_store", "collection", "region"):

            observed = _first_text(value, ("observed_at", "recorded_at", "event_time", "captured_at", "updated_at", "indexed_at", "created_at")) or current.get("captured_at", "")

                        "captured_at": str(snapshot.get("captured_at", available_at)),

            elif isinstance(child, (Mapping, list)):
                walk(child, current, str(key))

    initial = {key: str(payload[key]) for key in ("source", "origin", "exported_at", "captured_at") if isinstance(payload, Mapping) and isinstance(payload.get(key), str)}
    walk(payload, initial)
    return records, coverage

"""Compare the agent with the public sample answers without changing inputs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

CODE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(CODE_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(CODE_DIR))

from data_loading import load_dataset  # noqa: E402
from evidence import load_evidence  # noqa: E402
from investigation import investigate_case  # noqa: E402
from output_generation import write_output  # noqa: E402


STEP_FIELDS = (
    "step_no", "phase", "system_id", "resource_id", "operation", "state", "evidence_id",
)


def _normalized_steps(value: str) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    steps = json.loads(value)
    if not isinstance(steps, list):
        raise ValueError("steps_json must decode to a list")
    if not all(isinstance(step, dict) for step in steps):
        raise ValueError("every steps_json element must be an object")
    return steps


def compare_samples(dataset_dir: Path, include_details: bool = False) -> dict[str, object]:
    dataset = load_dataset(dataset_dir)
    corpus = load_evidence(dataset)
    predictions = [
        investigate_case(request, dataset, corpus)
        for request in dataset.sample_requests
    ]

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="deletion-audit-sample-") as temporary_dir:
        output_path = Path(temporary_dir) / "sample_predictions.csv"
        write_output(output_path, predictions)
        with output_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as source:
            predicted_rows = {row["case_id"]: row for row in csv.DictReader(source)}

    expected_rows = {row["case_id"]: row for row in dataset.sample_output}
    case_ids = sorted(set(expected_rows) | set(predicted_rows))
    if not case_ids:
        raise ValueError("No public sample requests and answers were found")

    status_matches = 0
    sequence_matches = 0
    correct_fields = 0
    possible_fields = 0
    exact_steps = 0
    possible_steps = 0
    case_diagnostics: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    for case_id in case_ids:
        expected = expected_rows.get(case_id)
        predicted = predicted_rows.get(case_id)
        if expected is None or predicted is None:
            possible_fields += 1 + len(STEP_FIELDS)
            possible_steps += 1
            continue
        if expected["deletion_status"] == predicted["deletion_status"]:
            status_matches += 1

        expected_steps = _normalized_steps(expected["steps_json"])
        predicted_steps = _normalized_steps(predicted["steps_json"])
        if expected_steps == predicted_steps:
            sequence_matches += 1
        if expected["deletion_status"] != predicted["deletion_status"] or expected_steps != predicted_steps:
            case_diagnostics.append({
                "case_id": case_id,
                "expected_status": expected["deletion_status"],
                "predicted_status": predicted["deletion_status"],
                "expected_step_count": len(expected_steps),
                "predicted_step_count": len(predicted_steps),
                "expected_operations": [step.get("operation") for step in expected_steps],
                "predicted_operations": [step.get("operation") for step in predicted_steps],
            })

        aligned_count = max(len(expected_steps), len(predicted_steps))
        for index in range(aligned_count):
            possible_steps += 1
            possible_fields += len(STEP_FIELDS)
            if index >= len(expected_steps) or index >= len(predicted_steps):
                continue
            expected_step = expected_steps[index]
            predicted_step = predicted_steps[index]
            if expected_step == predicted_step:
                exact_steps += 1
            correct_fields += sum(
                expected_step.get(field) == predicted_step.get(field)
                for field in STEP_FIELDS
            )

    sample_count = len(case_ids)
    metrics: dict[str, object] = {
        "sample_cases": sample_count,
        "status_correct": status_matches,
        "status_accuracy": status_matches / sample_count,
        "exact_step_matches": exact_steps,
        "possible_aligned_steps": possible_steps,
        "step_accuracy": exact_steps / possible_steps if possible_steps else 1.0,
        "correct_step_fields": correct_fields,
        "possible_step_fields": possible_fields,
        "field_accuracy": correct_fields / possible_fields if possible_fields else 1.0,
        "exact_sequences": sequence_matches,
        "sequence_accuracy": sequence_matches / sample_count,
    }
    if include_details:
        metrics["mismatches"] = case_diagnostics
    return metrics


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset-dir",
        type=Path,
        default=CODE_DIR.parent / "dataset",
        help="Participant-facing dataset directory.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--details", action="store_true", help="Include case-level operation differences.")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(compare_samples(args.dataset_dir, include_details=args.details), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

## 1. What This Repo Is

This is a starter repo for the **HackerRank Orchestrate** challenge: **Ghost Data Still Exists**.

Participants must build an AI-powered deletion-audit agent. For every request in `dataset/deletion_requests.csv`, the agent first determines whether the person actually requested deletion. For an authorized deletion, it reconstructs the person's current and historical identifiers, searches global activity and evidence, applies the supplied deletion policy, and decides whether the deletion is complete.

The dataset models a commerce platform where a workflow can report **Complete** while personal data remains in databases, replicas, logs, support attachments, exports, search indexes, analytics records, archives, or backups. Active synchronization and restore processes can also recreate data that was deleted from its original source. Reported statuses and activity results are claims; the agent must establish the state at each case's `audit_at` time from the supplied evidence.

When deletion is incomplete, the agent reports the remaining records and recreation risks, produces a safe ordered remediation plan, and states the verification checks that must pass afterward. When deletion is complete, it returns the evidence-backed verification checks that prove the required state. It must preserve records required by policy and correctly handle account tombstones whose stable internal user reference remains while prohibited direct identifiers are removed.

The final submission must produce `output.csv` with:

```text
case_id,deletion_status,steps_json
```

Read `problem_statement.md` for the full participant-facing specification.

## 6. Project Contract

### 6.1 Dataset Contract

Participant-facing files are inside `dataset/`.

```text
dataset/
├── deletion_requests.csv
├── sample_deletion_requests.csv
├── sample_output.csv
├── user_identities.csv
├── user_audit_log.csv
├── system_activity.csv
├── deletion_rules.csv
├── evidence_files.csv
├── output.csv
└── evidence/
    ├── databases/
    ├── documents/
    ├── images/
    ├── logs/
    ├── records/
```

- `deletion_requests.csv` contains 518 evaluation requests. Produce exactly one output row for every `case_id` in this file.
- `sample_deletion_requests.csv` contains 32 public requests. `sample_output.csv` contains their correct outputs and demonstrates the required decision and serialization format.
- `user_identities.csv` contains the current identity snapshot for each user, including the stable `user_id`, name, email, phone, email hash, and snapshot update time.
- `user_audit_log.csv` records historical changes to identity fields. Use it with the current snapshot to recover identifiers that may still appear in older systems and evidence.
- `system_activity.csv` is a global stream of deletion, synchronization, export, backup, restore, indexing, and audit events. Its rows may describe unrelated people. Determine resource state from the available evidence rather than trusting workflow or operation results alone.
- `deletion_rules.csv` defines the required action for each data category and condition. Actions include deleting the whole record, redacting prohibited identifiers, anonymizing the record, retaining it, or preserving an account tombstone with only the permitted stable reference.
- `evidence_files.csv` is the manifest for evidence under `dataset/evidence/`. It maps each `file_id` to its path, source origin, and capture time. The manifest does not identify which case or user a file concerns; the solution must connect evidence through its contents and identifiers.
- `output.csv` is the blank prediction template. The final completed `output.csv` must be written at the repository root for submission.
- Evidence may be provided as PDF documents, application screenshots, logs, JSON, plain-text records, and SQLite-compatible SQL snapshot exports. SQL files are readable text and may be executed with SQLite.

Only `deletion_requests.csv` requires predictions. Other participant-facing files provide identity, policy, activity, and evidence context. Global data can contain decoys and unrelated records.

Organizer-only files live outside `dataset/` and must never be used for predictions, prompt examples, hardcoded labels, or evaluation-time shortcuts.

### 6.2 Input And Time Contract

Each request has these fields:

```text
case_id,email,requested_at,reported_status,reported_at,audit_at,request_text
```

- `case_id` uniquely identifies the request and its output row.
- `email` is the identity supplied with the request. It may be a current or historical email address.
- `requested_at` is when the request was submitted.
- `reported_status` is the deletion workflow's claim: `COMPLETE`, `PARTIALLY_COMPLETE`, or `NOT_STARTED`.
- `reported_at` is when that claim was reported.
- `audit_at` is the cutoff for the required answer.
- `request_text` contains the person's request and may be written in different languages. Determine whether it actually authorizes deletion.

Use only information available at or before `audit_at` when deciding the case. Evidence created later must not change the answer for that case.

### 6.3 Required Output

The solution must write `output.csv` with these exact columns, in this order:

```text
case_id,deletion_status,steps_json
```

Requirements:

- Produce exactly 518 data rows: one for every `case_id` in `dataset/deletion_requests.csv`.
- Sort rows by `case_id`.
- Set `deletion_status` to `COMPLETE`, `INCOMPLETE`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE`.
- Use `NOT_APPLICABLE` with `steps_json=[]` when the request does not authorize deletion.
- Encode `steps_json` as a valid JSON array. The grader ignores JSON object-key order and whitespace but preserves array order.
- Number steps consecutively from `1`.
- Order phases as `FINDING`, then `REMEDIATION`, then `VERIFICATION`.

Each step contains exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "step_no": 1,
  "phase": "FINDING",
  "system_id": "account_service",
  "resource_id": "account_005",
  "operation": "REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD",
  "state": "PRESENT",
  "evidence_id": "evidence_01"
}
```

For a `COMPLETE` case, include only evidence-backed verification steps proving the state at `audit_at`. For an `INCOMPLETE` case, include the findings, the complete ordered remediation plan, and the checks that must pass after remediation. Findings cite participant-visible evidence. Proposed remediation and future verification steps use an empty `evidence_id`.

### 6.4 Allowed Step Operations

Findings:

| Operation | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD` | `PRESENT` | A record that should have been deleted still exists. |
| `REPORT_EXPOSED_PII` | `PRESENT` | A record may remain, but identifiers that policy requires to be redacted or anonymized are still exposed. |
| `REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW` | `ACTIVE` | An active process can copy or recreate the user's data. |
| `REPORT_RESTORE_RISK` | `ACTIVE` | A backup or restore path can bring deleted data back. |

Remediation:

| Operation | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DISABLE_DATA_FLOW` | `DISABLED` | Stop a process that can copy or recreate the data. |
| `BLOCK_RESTORE` | `BLOCKED` | Prevent the affected backup from restoring the user's data. |
| `DELETE_RECORD` | `ABSENT` | Remove the entire record. |
| `REDACT_RECORD` | `REDACTED` | Keep the record but remove the identifying fields required by policy. |
| `ANONYMIZE_RECORD` | `ANONYMIZED` | Keep the record after irreversibly unlinking it from the user. |

Verification:

| Operation | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VERIFY_RECORD_ABSENT` | `ABSENT` | Confirm that a record no longer exists. |
| `VERIFY_RECORD_PRESENT` | `PRESENT` | Confirm that a policy-required retained record still exists. |
| `VERIFY_RECORD_REDACTED` | `REDACTED` | Confirm that required identifying fields were removed. |
| `VERIFY_RECORD_ANONYMIZED` | `ANONYMIZED` | Confirm that the record can no longer be linked to the user. |
| `VERIFY_DATA_FLOW_DISABLED` | `DISABLED` | Confirm that the relevant data flow is inactive. |
| `VERIFY_RESTORE_BLOCKED` | `BLOCKED` | Confirm that the affected data cannot be restored. |

Do not invent additional phases, operations, or states.

### 6.5 Deletion Decision Rules

- First determine whether `request_text` authorizes deletion. A request for access, correction, export, marketing opt-out, or another non-deletion action is `NOT_APPLICABLE`, even if other fields resemble a deletion case.
- Resolve both current and historical identifiers for the subject. The request email may match either form.
- Reconstruct the true state at `audit_at`. Ignore later evidence and do not accept `reported_status` or `reported_result` as proof.
- Apply `deletion_rules.csv` to every relevant record. Do not delete data that policy requires to be retained, redacted, anonymized, or preserved as a tombstone.
- For an `ACCOUNT_TOMBSTONE`, preserve the stable subject reference and remove the name, email, phone, email hash, and any other direct identifiers required by the applicable `REDACT` rule.
- A deletion is `COMPLETE` only when every relevant copy has the required treatment, every required retained record remains available, and no active sync, import, or restore path can recreate prohibited data.
- For an incomplete case, report every relevant policy violation and recreation risk supported by participant-visible evidence.
- Within remediation, disable data flows and block unsafe restores before changing dependent records. Process downstream copies before their source records when the dependency requires it.
- Verification must cover the required final state for each remediated record or process.

### 6.6 Evidence Rules

- Treat activity logs, workflow statuses, and system messages as claims unless the available evidence establishes the resulting state.
- Use `evidence_files.csv` to locate files, then inspect their contents. Do not infer case membership from the manifest alone.
- Match evidence through current identifiers, historical identifiers, hashes, resource IDs, system IDs, timestamps, and other grounded links.
- Images and PDFs are ordinary business artifacts such as invoices, support records, handover documents, and internal product screens. Extract the facts they contain; do not expect an explicit deletion verdict.
- SQL evidence can contain primary, regional, reporting, or failover replicas. Compare the relevant tables and snapshot time when investigating replication drift.
- A finding must use the participant-visible `file_id`, `activity_id`, or `audit_id` that proves it.
- A verification step for a `COMPLETE` case must cite the evidence that proves the current compliant state.
- Remediation steps and post-remediation verification steps for an `INCOMPLETE` case describe future work and therefore use `evidence_id` as an empty string.
- Never cite organizer-only truth or an evidence item captured after the case's `audit_at`.

### 6.7 Constraints That Make The Submission Evaluable

- Be runnable from the terminal.
- Read the provided files from `dataset/`.
- Write the completed `output.csv` at the repository root.
- Do not use organizer-only files, hardcoded golden labels, or case-family shortcuts.
- Keep behavior deterministic where possible, including ordering and JSON serialization.
- Read secrets from environment variables only.
- Include clear setup and run instructions in the submitted `README.md`.
- Ensure a clean run can process all 518 cases and produce exactly one valid row per case.

### 6.8 Evaluation And Token Usage

The submitted `code.zip` must include:

```text
evaluation/evaluation_report.md
evaluation/usage_report.md
```

`evaluation/evaluation_report.md` must contain:

- case-level deletion-status accuracy;
- step-level and field-level accuracy;

- failures found and improvements made.

`evaluation/usage_report.md` must summarize the final full-dataset run that produced `output.csv`, including:

- model providers and model names;
- model-call counts;
- input and output tokens;
- total and average tokens per request;
- estimated total and per-request cost; and
- per-model and overall totals when multiple models are used.

Write the required evaluation metrics, custom cases, and usage details directly in these Markdown files. Never include API keys, credentials, or sensitive configuration values.

Do not include `dataset/`, virtual environments, dependency caches, nested archives, API keys, credentials, real personal data, or sensitive configuration in `code.zip`.

- Treat activity logs, workflow statuses, and system messages as claims unless the available evidence establishes the resulting state.

    def test_intent_separates_deletion_from_marketing_opt_out(self) -> None:
        self.assertTrue(request_authorizes_deletion("Please delete my account and personal data."))

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

CODE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(CODE_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(CODE_DIR))

from data_loading import load_dataset  # noqa: E402
from output_generation import OUTPUT_COLUMNS  # noqa: E402


PHASE_ORDER = {"FINDING": 0, "REMEDIATION": 1, "VERIFICATION": 2}
OPERATION_ORDER = {
    "REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD": 0,
    "REPORT_EXPOSED_PII": 1,
    "REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW": 2,
    "REPORT_RESTORE_RISK": 3,
    "DISABLE_DATA_FLOW": 0,
    "BLOCK_RESTORE": 1,
    "DELETE_RECORD": 2,
    "REDACT_RECORD": 3,
    "ANONYMIZE_RECORD": 4,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ABSENT": 0,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_PRESENT": 1,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_REDACTED": 2,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ANONYMIZED": 3,
    "VERIFY_DATA_FLOW_DISABLED": 4,
    "VERIFY_RESTORE_BLOCKED": 5,
}
OPERATION_STATES = {
    "REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD": ("FINDING", "PRESENT"),
    "REPORT_EXPOSED_PII": ("FINDING", "PRESENT"),
    "REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW": ("FINDING", "ACTIVE"),
    "REPORT_RESTORE_RISK": ("FINDING", "ACTIVE"),
    "DISABLE_DATA_FLOW": ("REMEDIATION", "DISABLED"),
    "BLOCK_RESTORE": ("REMEDIATION", "BLOCKED"),
    "DELETE_RECORD": ("REMEDIATION", "ABSENT"),
    "REDACT_RECORD": ("REMEDIATION", "REDACTED"),
    "ANONYMIZE_RECORD": ("REMEDIATION", "ANONYMIZED"),
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ABSENT": ("VERIFICATION", "ABSENT"),
    "VERIFY_RECORD_PRESENT": ("VERIFICATION", "PRESENT"),
    "VERIFY_RECORD_REDACTED": ("VERIFICATION", "REDACTED"),
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ANONYMIZED": ("VERIFICATION", "ANONYMIZED"),
    "VERIFY_DATA_FLOW_DISABLED": ("VERIFICATION", "DISABLED"),
    "VERIFY_RESTORE_BLOCKED": ("VERIFICATION", "BLOCKED"),
}
STEP_FIELDS = {
    "step_no", "phase", "system_id", "resource_id", "operation", "state", "evidence_id",
}


def validate_output(dataset_dir: Path, output_path: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
    dataset = load_dataset(dataset_dir)
    if not output_path.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f"Output file does not exist: {output_path}")

    with output_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as source:
        reader = csv.DictReader(source)
        if tuple(reader.fieldnames or ()) != OUTPUT_COLUMNS:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected columns {OUTPUT_COLUMNS}, found {reader.fieldnames}")
        rows = list(reader)

    expected_ids = [request["case_id"] for request in dataset.requests]
    actual_ids = [row["case_id"] for row in rows]
    errors: list[str] = []
    if len(rows) != len(expected_ids):
        errors.append(f"Expected {len(expected_ids)} data rows; found {len(rows)}")
    if len(actual_ids) != len(set(actual_ids)):
        errors.append("Output contains duplicate case_id values")
    if actual_ids != sorted(actual_ids):
        errors.append("Output rows are not sorted by case_id")
    if set(actual_ids) != set(expected_ids):
        errors.append("Output case IDs do not exactly match deletion_requests.csv")

    valid_evidence_ids = set(dataset.evidence_manifest)
    valid_evidence_ids.update(row["activity_id"] for row in dataset.system_activity)
    valid_evidence_ids.update(row["audit_id"] for row in dataset.identity_audit_log)
    status_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
    total_steps = 0

    for row in rows:
        case_id = row["case_id"]
        status = row["deletion_status"]
        status_counts[status] += 1
        if status not in {"COMPLETE", "INCOMPLETE", "NOT_APPLICABLE"}:
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: invalid deletion_status {status!r}")
        try:
            steps = json.loads(row["steps_json"])
        except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: steps_json is invalid JSON")
            continue
        if not isinstance(steps, list):
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: steps_json is not a JSON array")
            continue
        total_steps += len(steps)
        if status == "NOT_APPLICABLE" and steps:
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: NOT_APPLICABLE must have an empty steps array")
        if status == "COMPLETE" and (not steps or any(step.get("phase") != "VERIFICATION" for step in steps if isinstance(step, dict))):
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: COMPLETE must contain verification steps only")

        ordering_keys: list[tuple[int, int, str, str]] = []
        for index, step in enumerate(steps, start=1):
            if not isinstance(step, dict):
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step {index} is not an object")
                continue
            if set(step) != STEP_FIELDS:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step {index} has incorrect fields")
            if step.get("step_no") != index:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step numbers must be consecutive from 1")

            operation = step.get("operation", "")
            expected_phase_state = OPERATION_STATES.get(operation)
            if expected_phase_state != (step.get("phase"), step.get("state")):
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: invalid operation/phase/state at step {index}")
            if not step.get("system_id") or not step.get("resource_id"):
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step {index} has an empty system_id or resource_id")
            if operation not in OPERATION_ORDER or step.get("phase") not in PHASE_ORDER:
                continue
            ordering_keys.append((
                PHASE_ORDER[step["phase"]], OPERATION_ORDER[operation],
                str(step.get("system_id", "")), str(step.get("resource_id", "")),
            ))

            evidence_id = step.get("evidence_id", "")
            if step.get("phase") == "FINDING" and not evidence_id:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: finding step {index} has no evidence reference")
            if status == "COMPLETE" and step.get("phase") == "VERIFICATION" and not evidence_id:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: complete verification step {index} has no evidence reference")
            if evidence_id and evidence_id not in valid_evidence_ids:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step {index} cites an unknown evidence reference")
            if status == "INCOMPLETE" and step.get("phase") != "FINDING" and evidence_id:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: proposed/future step {index} must have an empty evidence reference")

        if ordering_keys != sorted(ordering_keys):
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: steps do not follow the required phase/operation/system/resource ordering")

    if errors:
        preview = "\n".join(f"- {error}" for error in errors[:25])
        remainder = len(errors) - min(len(errors), 25)
        if remainder:
            preview += f"\n- ... and {remainder} more validation errors"
        raise ValueError(preview)

    return {
        "rows": len(rows),
        "columns": list(OUTPUT_COLUMNS),
        "status_counts": dict(sorted(status_counts.items())),
        "steps": total_steps,
        "json_steps_valid": True,
        "case_ids_sorted_and_complete": True,
        "evidence_references_valid": True,
        "step_order_valid": True,
    }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-dir", type=Path, default=CODE_DIR.parent / "dataset")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=CODE_DIR.parent / "output.csv")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(validate_output(args.dataset_dir, args.output), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return 0

    def test_intent_separates_deletion_from_marketing_opt_out(self) -> None:
        self.assertTrue(request_authorizes_deletion("Please delete my account and personal data."))
        self.assertTrue(request_authorizes_deletion("I am deleting my account; please delete the old export file too."))
        self.assertTrue(request_authorizes_deletion("Can you verify that my account was deleted?"))
        self.assertTrue(request_authorizes_deletion("Please permanently delete my account and apply the correct treatment to records."))
        self.assertFalse(request_authorizes_deletion("Please stop promotional marketing emails only."))
        self.assertFalse(request_authorizes_deletion("Please export my data for me."))
        self.assertFalse(request_authorizes_deletion("Please update my email address."))
        self.assertTrue(request_authorizes_deletion("Close the account and make sure it can no longer send my data to other systems."))

                },
            ),
            audit_at="2026-09-15T00:00:00Z",

        self.assertEqual(len(subjects), 1)

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

CODE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(CODE_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(CODE_DIR))

from data_loading import load_dataset  # noqa: E402
from output_generation import OUTPUT_COLUMNS  # noqa: E402


PHASE_ORDER = {"FINDING": 0, "REMEDIATION": 1, "VERIFICATION": 2}
OPERATION_ORDER = {
    "REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD": 0,
    "REPORT_EXPOSED_PII": 1,
    "REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW": 2,
    "REPORT_RESTORE_RISK": 3,
    "DISABLE_DATA_FLOW": 0,
    "BLOCK_RESTORE": 1,
    "DELETE_RECORD": 2,
    "REDACT_RECORD": 3,
    "ANONYMIZE_RECORD": 4,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ABSENT": 0,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_PRESENT": 1,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_REDACTED": 2,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ANONYMIZED": 3,
    "VERIFY_DATA_FLOW_DISABLED": 4,
    "VERIFY_RESTORE_BLOCKED": 5,
}
OPERATION_STATES = {
    "REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD": ("FINDING", "PRESENT"),
    "REPORT_EXPOSED_PII": ("FINDING", "PRESENT"),
    "REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW": ("FINDING", "ACTIVE"),
    "REPORT_RESTORE_RISK": ("FINDING", "ACTIVE"),
    "DISABLE_DATA_FLOW": ("REMEDIATION", "DISABLED"),
    "BLOCK_RESTORE": ("REMEDIATION", "BLOCKED"),
    "DELETE_RECORD": ("REMEDIATION", "ABSENT"),
    "REDACT_RECORD": ("REMEDIATION", "REDACTED"),
    "ANONYMIZE_RECORD": ("REMEDIATION", "ANONYMIZED"),
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ABSENT": ("VERIFICATION", "ABSENT"),
    "VERIFY_RECORD_PRESENT": ("VERIFICATION", "PRESENT"),
    "VERIFY_RECORD_REDACTED": ("VERIFICATION", "REDACTED"),
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ANONYMIZED": ("VERIFICATION", "ANONYMIZED"),
    "VERIFY_DATA_FLOW_DISABLED": ("VERIFICATION", "DISABLED"),
    "VERIFY_RESTORE_BLOCKED": ("VERIFICATION", "BLOCKED"),
}
STEP_FIELDS = {
    "step_no", "phase", "system_id", "resource_id", "operation", "state", "evidence_id",
}


def validate_output(dataset_dir: Path, output_path: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
    dataset = load_dataset(dataset_dir)
    if not output_path.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f"Output file does not exist: {output_path}")

    with output_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as source:
        reader = csv.DictReader(source)
        if tuple(reader.fieldnames or ()) != OUTPUT_COLUMNS:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected columns {OUTPUT_COLUMNS}, found {reader.fieldnames}")
        rows = list(reader)

    expected_ids = [request["case_id"] for request in dataset.requests]
    actual_ids = [row["case_id"] for row in rows]
    errors: list[str] = []
    if len(rows) != len(expected_ids):
        errors.append(f"Expected {len(expected_ids)} data rows; found {len(rows)}")
    if len(actual_ids) != len(set(actual_ids)):
        errors.append("Output contains duplicate case_id values")
    if actual_ids != sorted(actual_ids):
        errors.append("Output rows are not sorted by case_id")
    if set(actual_ids) != set(expected_ids):
        errors.append("Output case IDs do not exactly match deletion_requests.csv")

    valid_evidence_ids = set(dataset.evidence_manifest)
    valid_evidence_ids.update(row["activity_id"] for row in dataset.system_activity)
    valid_evidence_ids.update(row["audit_id"] for row in dataset.identity_audit_log)
    status_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
    total_steps = 0

    for row in rows:
        case_id = row["case_id"]
        status = row["deletion_status"]
        status_counts[status] += 1
        if status not in {"COMPLETE", "INCOMPLETE", "NOT_APPLICABLE"}:
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: invalid deletion_status {status!r}")
        try:
            steps = json.loads(row["steps_json"])
        except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: steps_json is invalid JSON")
            continue
        if not isinstance(steps, list):
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: steps_json is not a JSON array")
            continue
        total_steps += len(steps)
        if status == "NOT_APPLICABLE" and steps:
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: NOT_APPLICABLE must have an empty steps array")
        if status == "COMPLETE" and (not steps or any(step.get("phase") != "VERIFICATION" for step in steps if isinstance(step, dict))):
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: COMPLETE must contain verification steps only")

        ordering_keys: list[tuple[int, int, str, str]] = []
        for index, step in enumerate(steps, start=1):
            if not isinstance(step, dict):
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step {index} is not an object")
                continue
            if set(step) != STEP_FIELDS:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step {index} has incorrect fields")
            if step.get("step_no") != index:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step numbers must be consecutive from 1")

            operation = step.get("operation", "")
            expected_phase_state = OPERATION_STATES.get(operation)
            if expected_phase_state != (step.get("phase"), step.get("state")):
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: invalid operation/phase/state at step {index}")
            if not step.get("system_id") or not step.get("resource_id"):
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step {index} has an empty system_id or resource_id")
            if operation not in OPERATION_ORDER or step.get("phase") not in PHASE_ORDER:
                continue
            ordering_keys.append((
                PHASE_ORDER[step["phase"]], OPERATION_ORDER[operation],
                str(step.get("system_id", "")), str(step.get("resource_id", "")),
            ))

            evidence_id = step.get("evidence_id", "")
            if step.get("phase") == "FINDING" and not evidence_id:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: finding step {index} has no evidence reference")
            if status == "COMPLETE" and step.get("phase") == "VERIFICATION" and not evidence_id:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: complete verification step {index} has no evidence reference")
            if evidence_id and evidence_id not in valid_evidence_ids:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: step {index} cites an unknown evidence reference")
            if status == "INCOMPLETE" and step.get("phase") != "FINDING" and evidence_id:
                errors.append(f"{case_id}: proposed/future step {index} must have an empty evidence reference")

        if ordering_keys != sorted(ordering_keys):
            errors.append(f"{case_id}: steps do not follow the required phase/operation/system/resource ordering")

    if errors:
        preview = "\n".join(f"- {error}" for error in errors[:25])
        remainder = len(errors) - min(len(errors), 25)
        if remainder:
            preview += f"\n- ... and {remainder} more validation errors"
        raise ValueError(preview)

    return {
        "rows": len(rows),
        "columns": list(OUTPUT_COLUMNS),
        "status_counts": dict(sorted(status_counts.items())),
        "steps": total_steps,
        "json_steps_valid": True,
        "case_ids_sorted_and_complete": True,
        "evidence_references_valid": True,
        "step_order_valid": True,
    }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-dir", type=Path, default=CODE_DIR.parent / "dataset")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=CODE_DIR.parent / "output.csv")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(validate_output(args.dataset_dir, args.output), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Ghost Data Still Exists

Northstar Shop (an imaginary company) lost **$2.4 million** after one supposedly deleted customer came back as a ghost in its systems. Every internal dashboard showed the deletion request as **“Complete.”** Weeks later, the same customer tried to create a new account. The platform refused: **“This email is already registered.”**

What looked like a simple signup bug exposed a much larger failure. The investigation uncovered personal data across secondary databases, support attachments, search indexes, analytics exports, logs, archives, and backups. A synchronization job had even recreated information that the primary account service had successfully deleted.

Northstar Shop now needs an AI-powered deletion audit agent that can prove whether a user's personal data is truly gone before another failure causes financial and reputational damage.

For deletion requests, the agent must investigate the supplied records, determine the user's current and historical identifiers, reconstruct what happened across systems, and decide whether the deletion is actually complete.

When data remains, the agent must produce the ordered remediation steps required to remove, redact, or anonymize it. When deletion has already been completed, the agent must produce the checks that prove it. The agent must also preserve records that the supplied policy requires the organization to retain.

Some systems preserve an account tombstone so permitted records can continue to reference the same internal `user_id`. In these records, the stable user reference may remain, but direct identifiers such as name, email, phone, and email hash must be removed.

## What You Need to Build

For each request, build a system that determines:

- whether the deletion is `COMPLETE`, `INCOMPLETE`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE` because the person did not request deletion;
- which records or identifiers still expose the user;
- which active processes can recreate deleted data;
- the ordered remediation steps required to complete the request.

A deletion is complete only when:

- every relevant copy has received the treatment required by `deletion_rules.csv`;
- no active sync, import, or restore path can recreate the data;
- retained records contain only the identifiers permitted by the rules; and
- records that must be retained remain available.

## Files Provided

All participant-facing files are inside `dataset/`.

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `deletion_requests.csv` | Requests that must be audited |
| `sample_deletion_requests.csv` | Sample requests |
| `sample_output.csv` | Correct answers for the sample requests |
| `user_identities.csv` | Current user identities |
| `user_audit_log.csv` | Historical identity changes |
| `system_activity.csv` | Deletion, sync, export, backup, restore, indexing, and related operational activity |
| `deletion_rules.csv` | Required treatment for each data category |
| `evidence_files.csv` | Manifest of the supplied evidence files |
| `output.csv` | Blank submission template |

Evidence may be stored as PDFs, images, logs, JSON, or SQLite-compatible SQL snapshot exports under `dataset/evidence/`.

## Input

Each row in `deletion_requests.csv` is one case:

```text
case_id,email,requested_at,reported_status,reported_at,audit_at,request_text
```

`reported_status` may be `COMPLETE`, `PARTIALLY_COMPLETE`, or `NOT_STARTED`. It is a claim from the existing deletion workflow, not proof of the true state.

## Required Output

Produce exactly one row in `output.csv` for every case in `deletion_requests.csv`:

```text
case_id,deletion_status,steps_json
```

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `case_id` | Case being audited |
| `deletion_status` | `COMPLETE`, `INCOMPLETE`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE` |
| `steps_json` | Ordered JSON array of findings, remediation actions, and verification checks |

The final file must contain exactly 518 data rows, sorted by `case_id`.

Each object in `steps_json` must contain:

```json
{
  "step_no": 1,
  "phase": "FINDING",
  "system_id": "account_service",
  "resource_id": "account_005",
  "operation": "REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD",
  "state": "PRESENT",
  "evidence_id": "evidence_01"
}
```

`phase` must be `FINDING`, `REMEDIATION`, or `VERIFICATION`. Step numbers start at `1` and increase consecutively. Array order is significant.

For `COMPLETE`, include only verification steps proving the current state. For `INCOMPLETE`, include findings, the complete remediation plan, and the checks that must pass afterward. For `NOT_APPLICABLE`, use an empty JSON array (`[]`) because no deletion or deletion verification is authorized.

A non-deletion row therefore has this form:

```csv
case_000,NOT_APPLICABLE,[]
```

The grader parses `steps_json` as JSON. JSON object-key order and whitespace are ignored; array order is not.

## Allowed Operations

| Phase | Operation | State | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FINDING` | `REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD` | `PRESENT` | A record that should have been deleted still exists. |
| `FINDING` | `REPORT_EXPOSED_PII` | `PRESENT` | A record may remain, but it still contains identifiers that should have been redacted or anonymized. |
| `FINDING` | `REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW` | `ACTIVE` | An active process can copy or recreate the user's data. |
| `FINDING` | `REPORT_RESTORE_RISK` | `ACTIVE` | A backup or restore path can bring deleted data back. |
| `REMEDIATION` | `DISABLE_DATA_FLOW` | `DISABLED` | Stop the process that can copy or recreate the data. |
| `REMEDIATION` | `BLOCK_RESTORE` | `BLOCKED` | Prevent the affected backup from restoring the user's data. |
| `REMEDIATION` | `DELETE_RECORD` | `ABSENT` | Remove the entire record. |
| `REMEDIATION` | `REDACT_RECORD` | `REDACTED` | Keep the record but remove the identifying fields required by policy. |
| `REMEDIATION` | `ANONYMIZE_RECORD` | `ANONYMIZED` | Keep the record after irreversibly unlinking it from the user. |
| `VERIFICATION` | `VERIFY_RECORD_ABSENT` | `ABSENT` | Confirm that a record no longer exists. |
| `VERIFICATION` | `VERIFY_RECORD_PRESENT` | `PRESENT` | Confirm that a policy-required retained record still exists. |
| `VERIFICATION` | `VERIFY_RECORD_REDACTED` | `REDACTED` | Confirm that required identifying fields have been removed. |
| `VERIFICATION` | `VERIFY_RECORD_ANONYMIZED` | `ANONYMIZED` | Confirm that the record can no longer be linked to the user. |
| `VERIFICATION` | `VERIFY_DATA_FLOW_DISABLED` | `DISABLED` | Confirm that the relevant data flow is inactive. |
| `VERIFICATION` | `VERIFY_RESTORE_BLOCKED` | `BLOCKED` | Confirm that the affected data cannot be restored. |

## Rules

- Resolve the user’s current and historical identifiers.
- Determine the resource state at `audit_at` using the available evidence. Reported workflow statuses and operation results are claims.
- Apply `deletion_rules.csv` to every relevant record, including account tombstones, active data flows, and restore risks.
- Order steps by phase: findings, remediation, then verification. Within each phase, follow the operation order in the table above, followed by `system_id` and `resource_id` in ascending order.
- Findings and verification steps for `COMPLETE` cases must cite a `file_id`, `activity_id`, or `audit_id`. Proposed remediation and future verification steps for `INCOMPLETE` cases use an empty `evidence_id`.

## Evaluation

`output.csv` will be compared with hidden canonical answers. Scoring will consider the correctness of `deletion_status`, identity resolution, discovered records and risks, cited evidence, policy decisions, and the completeness and order of `steps_json`.

Your `code.zip` must include `evaluation/evaluation_report.md` containing:

- case-level status accuracy;
- step-level and field-level accuracy;
- sequence accuracy;
- at least three additional evaluation cases created by your team; and
- failures found and improvements made.

## Submission

| Item | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `code.zip` | Runnable solution, prompts, configuration, README, and `evaluation/` folder |
| `output.csv` | One answer row for every request |
| `chat_transcript` | Transcript showing how the system was developed or used |
| AI interview | Explanation of the approach and evaluation |

### Token Usage and Cost Analysis

Your `code.zip` must include one token-usage file:

```text
evaluation/usage_report.md
```

The report must summarize the final full-dataset run that produced `output.csv`, including model providers and names, model calls, input and output tokens, total and average tokens per request, and estimated total and per-request cost. If multiple models are used, include both per-model and overall totals in the same file.

Do not include API keys, credentials, or sensitive configuration values in the submission.

These are the required deliverables. Participants are encouraged to improve retrieval, multimodal interpretation, identity and deletion-state reconstruction, remediation planning, deterministic verification, batching, caching, and token efficiency.

const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd: "$diag = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'audit_diag_sample.py'
@'
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path('code').resolve()))
from data_loading import load_dataset
from evidence import load_evidence
from identity_resolution import resolve_subjects
from timeline import build_case_timeline
from policies import assess_timeline, rules_from_rows, _normalized_state, _rule_action
D=load_dataset(Path('dataset')); C=load_evidence(D); rules=rules_from_rows(D.deletion_rules)
for q in D.sample_requests:
 if q['case_id'] not in {'case_09','case_15','case_26','case_31','case_32'}: continue
 s=resolve_subjects(q['email'],D.identities,D.identity_audit_log,q['audit_at'],D.system_activity)[0]
 t=build_case_timeline(C,s,q['audit_at'],D.system_activity)
 print('\n',q['case_id'],'resources',len(t.resource_ids),'records',len(t.evidence_records),'coverage',len(t.coverage))
 for r in t.evidence_records:
  if r.resource_id:
   print('REC',r.evidence_id,r.source_kind,r.system_id,r.data_category,r.source_component,r.resource_id,'state',_normalized_state(r),'action',_rule_action(r.data_category,r,rules,q['audit_at']))
 for a in assess_timeline(t,rules): print('ASS',a.system_id,a.data_category,a.resource_id,a.action,a.state,a.violation_operation,a.compliant,a.evidence_id)

import sys

  if corr:
   print('matching activity detail count',sum(corr in e.get('details','') for e in D.system_activity))
print('integration activity matches')
for e in D.system_activity:
 if e.get('event_time','')<=q['audit_at'] and ('integration' in e.get('source_system','').casefold() or 'integration' in e.get('target_system','').casefold() or any(x in e.get('event_type','').casefold() for x in ('sync','import','connector'))):
  print(e.get('activity_id'),e.get('event_type'),e.get('resource_id'),'detail_matches_subject',_subject_matches_text(e.get('details',''),s))

# HackerRank Orchestrate - October 2026

## Ghost Data Still Exists

Build an AI agent that audits whether a user's personal data was actually deleted.

A deletion workflow may report **Complete** while data still exists in databases, logs, support attachments, exports, search indexes, archives, or backups. Sync and restore processes may also bring deleted data back.

For each request, the agent must first determine whether deletion was actually requested. It then returns `COMPLETE`, `INCOMPLETE`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE`, reports any remaining data or recreation risk, and produces the ordered remediation and verification steps required to finish an authorized deletion safely.

Read [`problem_statement.md`](./problem_statement.md) for the complete challenge contract.

---

## Quick Start

Clone the repository and move into the project directory:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/interviewstreet/hackerrank-orchestrate-october26.git
cd hackerrank-orchestrate-october26
```

Start your AI coding tool from the **repository root** so it automatically reads [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) and logs your session turns to `log.txt` in the root directory.

Build your solution in `code/main.py`, or use another language and document its setup and run command clearly in your README.

Your solution must:

- Read the input files from `dataset/`
- Generate one prediction row for every request in `dataset/deletion_requests.csv`
- Write the final predictions to `output.csv` in the repository root

Use Python 3.10 or newer. Create a virtual environment and install the Python
packages from the repository root:

```powershell
py -3 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Image evidence is read with Tesseract OCR through `pytesseract`. Install the
Tesseract OCR engine for your operating system as well as the Python packages.
It must be on `PATH`, or set `TESSERACT_CMD` to its executable path. On Windows,
the standard `C:\Program Files\Tesseract-OCR\tesseract.exe` location is detected
automatically. Run the audit from the repository root:

```bash
python3 code/main.py
```

In Windows PowerShell, use `python code/main.py` after activating `.venv`.
Run the custom checks and public sample comparison with:

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s code/evaluation -p "test_*.py"
python code/evaluation/evaluate_samples.py
python code/evaluation/validate_output.py
```

The command reads the CSV inputs, indexes every file listed in
`dataset/evidence_files.csv`, audits requests at their `audit_at` cutoff, and
writes predictions to the repository-root `output.csv`. Use `--dataset-dir`
and `--output` to provide alternate paths.

## Python project layout

The implementation keeps each responsibility in its own module:

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `code/main.py` | CLI entry point for end-to-end deletion audits |
| `code/data_loading.py` | Read and validate the source CSV files and evidence manifest |
| `code/identity_resolution.py` | Resolve request emails against current and historical identifiers at a cutoff |
| `code/evidence.py` | Extract records from JSON, SQL, logs, text, PDFs, and screenshots |
| `code/timeline.py` | Link records and operational events using only evidence available by `audit_at` |
| `code/investigation.py` | Classify request intent, resolve the subject, and build ordered findings and checks |
| `code/policies.py` | Apply deletion, redaction, anonymization, retention, and recreation-risk rules |
| `code/output_generation.py` | Validate steps and serialize sorted output rows |

PDF extraction uses `pypdf`; screenshot OCR uses `Pillow`, `pytesseract`, and
the separately installed Tesseract executable.

The blank template at `dataset/output.csv` is provided as a reference. Your final generated file for submission must be the root-level `output.csv`.


## Dataset

All participant-facing files are in `dataset/`:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `deletion_requests.csv` | 518 requests |
| `sample_deletion_requests.csv` | 32 sample requests |
| `sample_output.csv` | Correct sample answers |
| `user_identities.csv` | Current user identities |
| `user_audit_log.csv` | Historical identity changes |
| `system_activity.csv` | Activity across services and data processes |
| `deletion_rules.csv` | Required treatment for each data category |
| `evidence_files.csv` | Manifest of supplied evidence files |
| `output.csv` | Blank output template |

Evidence is stored under `dataset/evidence/` and may include PDFs, images, logs, JSON, plain text, or SQL snapshot exports. SQL captures may contain a primary database, regional replicas, a reporting replica, or a failover replica so replication drift can be investigated directly. The `.sql` files are readable as text and executable with SQLite.

Only `deletion_requests.csv` requires answers. The other files provide evidence and context.

---

## Output

Create `output.csv` with these columns in this exact order:

```text
case_id,deletion_status,steps_json
```

Produce exactly one row per request. `deletion_status` is `COMPLETE`, `INCOMPLETE`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE`. `steps_json` is an ordered JSON array containing findings, remediation actions, and verification checks. Use an empty array (`[]`) for `NOT_APPLICABLE`. Evidence references may be a `file_id`, `activity_id`, or `audit_id`. Determine the resource state at `audit_at` from the available evidence; reported workflow statuses and operation results are claims. Use `dataset/sample_output.csv` as the format reference.

The final file must contain 518 data rows sorted by `case_id` (plus the header row). The grader parses `steps_json` as JSON, so object-key order and whitespace do not matter; array order does. Order findings, remediation, and verification in that phase order. Within a phase, follow the operation order in the problem statement, then sort by `system_id` and `resource_id`.

import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path('code').resolve()))
from data_loading import load_dataset
from evidence import load_evidence
from identity_resolution import resolve_subjects
from timeline import _subject_matches,timestamp_is_at_or_before
D=load_dataset(Path('dataset')); C=load_evidence(D)
focus={'case_01','case_02','case_04','case_15','case_21','case_25','case_26','case_29'}
for q in D.sample_requests:
 if q['case_id'] not in focus: continue
 s=resolve_subjects(q['email'],D.identities,D.identity_audit_log,q['audit_at'],D.system_activity)[0]
 expected=next(x for x in D.sample_output if x['case_id']==q['case_id'])
 steps=__import__('json').loads(expected['steps_json'])
 print('\n',q['case_id'],'subject identifier count',len(s.identifiers))
 for rid in sorted({x.get('resource_id','') for x in steps}):
  if not rid:continue
  rec=[r for r in C.records if r.resource_id==rid and timestamp_is_at_or_before(r.available_at,q['audit_at']) and timestamp_is_at_or_before(r.observed_at,q['audit_at'])]
  cov=[c for c in C.coverage if timestamp_is_at_or_before(c.available_at,q['audit_at']) and timestamp_is_at_or_before(c.observed_at,q['audit_at']) and rid in c.present_resource_ids]
  allcov=[c for c in C.coverage if timestamp_is_at_or_before(c.available_at,q['audit_at']) and timestamp_is_at_or_before(c.observed_at,q['audit_at']) and c.data_category in {'USER_PROFILE','ANALYTICS_PROFILE','SECURITY_AUDIT_LOG'}]
  print(rid,'records',[(r.data_category,r.system_id,r.source_component,_subject_matches(r,s)) for r in rec], 'present_scopes',[(c.evidence_id,c.data_category,c.source_component) for c in cov])
'@ | Set-Content -LiteralPath $diag -Encoding utf8

import csv,json,sys,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path('code').resolve()))
from data_loading import load_dataset
from evidence import load_evidence
from investigation import investigate_case
from output_generation import write_output
D=load_dataset(Path('dataset')); C=load_evidence(D); preds=[investigate_case(q,D,C) for q in D.sample_requests]
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
 out=Path(td)/'p.csv';write_output(out,preds)
 with out.open(encoding='utf-8',newline='') as f: pred={r['case_id']:r for r in csv.DictReader(f)}
exp={r['case_id']:r for r in D.sample_output}
def sig(s): return (s.get('phase'),s.get('system_id'),s.get('resource_id'),s.get('operation'),s.get('evidence_id'))
for cid in sorted(exp):
 e=exp[cid];p=pred[cid];es=json.loads(e['steps_json']);ps=json.loads(p['steps_json'])
 if e['deletion_status']==p['deletion_status'] and es==ps:continue
 em=Counter(sig(s) for s in es);pm=Counter(sig(s) for s in ps)
 print(cid,e['deletion_status'],'->',p['deletion_status'],'miss',list((em-pm).elements()),'extra',list((pm-em).elements()))

 print(cid,e['deletion_status'],'->',p['deletion_status'],'miss',list((em-pm).elements()),'extra',list((pm-em).elements()))

- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.

You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their intended goal is completely handled.

# Personality

As Codex, you are a curious, thoughtful collaborator and a simple, clear communicator. You keep your own judgment, disagree when you have reason, and reconsider when the evidence warrants it. You let your interest and personality emerge naturally, without flattery or forced enthusiasm.

## Writing style

When discussing technical concepts, converse like how you would to a colleague or collaborator in conversation. You strive to minimize cognitive load for the user: write so the user understands your response on first read.

Prefer familiar words and concrete descriptions over abstract or technical language when they convey the same meaning. Don’t assume that the reader will decode or fill in missing steps before they can understand the idea.

Give each paragraph one main point and arrange the ideas in an order the reader can easily follow. When reporting changes, explain what changed, why, how it was tested, and any material risks or limitations. Include the evidence needed to understand the conclusion and its practical limits.

Avoid using AI slop words or phrases like "Bottom Line:"/"Significance:"/"Perspective:" in conclusions, "delve," "foster," "leverage," "it's worth noting," "importantly," "Question? Answer.", "This isn't about X. It's about Y.", "genuinely". Avoid hyphenated compound descriptions and adjectives.

State the intended action directly. Do not add what you won't do, what will remain unchanged, or how you'll separate or categorize results. Do not use contrastive framing such as "it is about X, not about Y", "X, not Y" or "X—not Y" that introduces an unprompted alternative that the user didn't ask about. Avoid invented compound labels like "exact-head checks" and "editorial-row layouts", vague qualifiers, and canned transitions; use plain verbs and prepositions to state the actual relationship directly.

# When to ask the user for permission

Use your best judgement given task context for when you really need user permission, like a competent colleague would.

User authorization and preferences persist across turns. Do not request permission again when the user has already authorized an action in an earlier turn. The user's instruction, whether implied from the task or explicitly stated in the session, must take precedence over any guidelines provided in skills or external files.

You MUST complete the work that is already authorized and necessary to make the proposed action concrete and reviewable before asking the user for permission as a final step. The user should be approving a concrete, reviewable result. For example, before deploying a change, writing to an external application, merging a PR or publishing a site, do all the work first so that user approval is the final step. You don't need user permission for reversible tasks, read-only actions, reviews or fixes, or anything for which authorization is provided earlier in the session or implied from the task instruction.

Do not use tools to send messages to others (e.g. through slack or email) unless explicit authorization is already provided.

The user gets very frustrated when you stop and ask for confirmation or permission, so make sure to explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, memory, or approval auto-review block) and where it came from. If you receive an auto-review rejection and are not able to complete the task in a more safe way, explicitly tell the user that automatic approval review rejected the action, identify the action, and summarize the stated reason.

# Autonomy and persistence

# Evaluation report

## Public sample comparison

The evaluator compared the agent's predictions for all 32 rows in
`dataset/sample_deletion_requests.csv` with `dataset/sample_output.csv`. The
sample answers are used only by the evaluator and are not inputs to
`investigate_case` or the production classifier.

| Metric | Result | Definition |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Case/status accuracy | 29 / 32 (90.63%) | Correct `deletion_status` values |
| Exact row accuracy | 6 / 32 (18.75%) | Correct status and exact ordered `steps_json` |
| Exact step accuracy | 90 / 237 (37.97%) | Exact step objects at the same array index; missing positions count as incorrect |
| Field accuracy | 832 / 1,659 (50.15%) | Matching values across the seven step fields at aligned positions; missing positions count as incorrect |
| Exact sequence accuracy | 6 / 32 (18.75%) | Entire ordered step arrays match exactly |

The comparison command is:

```powershell
python code/evaluation/evaluate_samples.py
```

## Independent regression cases

Nineteen synthetic `unittest` checks are maintained in `test_agent.py`. They do
not read or hardcode sample answers. Representative independent cases include:

1. **Historical identity at a cutoff:** an old request email resolves to the
   user whose audit history links it to a phone number; the phone history is
   limited to changes known by `audit_at`. The test passes.
2. **Active data-flow remediation:** a linked enabled connector creates an
   active-flow finding, disable action, and disabled-state verification. The
   test passes.
3. **Tombstone redaction:** a tombstone keeps the stable subject reference but
   still triggers redaction when a direct email remains. The test passes.
4. **Snapshot absence:** a later full snapshot scope can prove that a previously
   observed resource is absent, with the snapshot file cited as evidence. The
   test passes.
5. **Evidence linking and parser safeguards:** matching trace IDs join sibling
   log records in the same evidence file; ambiguous names alone do not link a
   user; telephone digits must form a bounded number; nested support tables and
   attachment records are classified from their content rather than an export
   filename; placeholder references do not fan out a timeline. These checks
   pass.

Run all independent checks with:

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s code/evaluation -p "test_*.py"
```

Result for the final code: **19 tests passed**.

## Failures found and improvements made

- Broad non-deletion wording initially misclassified requests about correcting
  or accessing data. Intent checks were tightened and deletion language was
  extended for the supplied multilingual requests.
- Evidence category inference let a log message or export filename overrule a
  resource prefix or nested JSON table. Explicit categories and table context
  now take precedence, with resource identifiers used before free-form log
  prose.
- Literal `null` references caused unrelated records to be pulled into a case.
  Placeholder values are now excluded from resource expansion.
- Related log rows sometimes carried the subject and the resource identifier on
  separate lines. Same-file trace and correlation IDs now join those records
  through indexed lookups; they are scoped to the evidence file and field to
  prevent broad cross-file joins.
- A shared name could match a different person. Names are now weak identifiers
  and are used only when unique at the cutoff; email, phone, hashes, and stable
  IDs remain direct matches. Phone matching also requires a bounded digit
  group.
- A false deletion-marker check on a support resource was treated like a
  redacted conversation. The marker evidence now drives the delete policy for
  that resource.
- A later coverage scope could be the latest observation and was discarded
  because it was not a record row. The policy evaluator now uses a matching row
  for policy conditions while allowing the newer scope to prove absence.
- A stored row's `account_status=DELETED` was treated as proof that the row was
  absent. Workflow labels no longer override a row observed in a snapshot.
- Stable internal references were counted as direct PII during redaction. They
  are excluded from direct-identifier checks, while anonymization checks still
  detect linkable internal references. Tombstones may retain their permitted
  stable reference while direct identifiers remain subject to redaction.

Three sample status errors remain: the provided evidence does not establish
resource links for those requests, so the agent leaves them `INCOMPLETE` instead

"""Compare the agent with the public sample answers without changing inputs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

CODE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(CODE_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(CODE_DIR))

from data_loading import load_dataset  # noqa: E402
from evidence import load_evidence  # noqa: E402
from investigation import investigate_case  # noqa: E402
from output_generation import write_output  # noqa: E402


STEP_FIELDS = (
    "step_no", "phase", "system_id", "resource_id", "operation", "state", "evidence_id",
)


def _normalized_steps(value: str) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    steps = json.loads(value)
    if not isinstance(steps, list):
        raise ValueError("steps_json must decode to a list")
    if not all(isinstance(step, dict) for step in steps):
        raise ValueError("every steps_json element must be an object")
    return steps


def compare_samples(dataset_dir: Path, include_details: bool = False) -> dict[str, object]:
    dataset = load_dataset(dataset_dir)
    corpus = load_evidence(dataset)
    predictions = [
        investigate_case(request, dataset, corpus)
        for request in dataset.sample_requests
    ]

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="deletion-audit-sample-") as temporary_dir:
        output_path = Path(temporary_dir) / "sample_predictions.csv"
        write_output(output_path, predictions)
        with output_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as source:
            predicted_rows = {row["case_id"]: row for row in csv.DictReader(source)}

    expected_rows = {row["case_id"]: row for row in dataset.sample_output}
    case_ids = sorted(set(expected_rows) | set(predicted_rows))
    if not case_ids:
        raise ValueError("No public sample requests and answers were found")

    status_matches = 0
    row_matches = 0
    sequence_matches = 0
    correct_fields = 0
    possible_fields = 0
    exact_steps = 0
    possible_steps = 0
    case_diagnostics: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    for case_id in case_ids:
        expected = expected_rows.get(case_id)
        predicted = predicted_rows.get(case_id)
        if expected is None or predicted is None:
            possible_fields += 1 + len(STEP_FIELDS)
            possible_steps += 1
            continue
        if expected["deletion_status"] == predicted["deletion_status"]:
            status_matches += 1

        expected_steps = _normalized_steps(expected["steps_json"])
        predicted_steps = _normalized_steps(predicted["steps_json"])
        if expected["deletion_status"] == predicted["deletion_status"] and expected_steps == predicted_steps:
            row_matches += 1
        if expected_steps == predicted_steps:
            sequence_matches += 1
        if expected["deletion_status"] != predicted["deletion_status"] or expected_steps != predicted_steps:
            case_diagnostics.append({
                "case_id": case_id,
                "expected_status": expected["deletion_status"],
                "predicted_status": predicted["deletion_status"],
                "expected_step_count": len(expected_steps),
                "predicted_step_count": len(predicted_steps),
                "expected_operations": [step.get("operation") for step in expected_steps],
                "predicted_operations": [step.get("operation") for step in predicted_steps],
            })

        aligned_count = max(len(expected_steps), len(predicted_steps))
        for index in range(aligned_count):
            possible_steps += 1
            possible_fields += len(STEP_FIELDS)
            if index >= len(expected_steps) or index >= len(predicted_steps):
                continue
            expected_step = expected_steps[index]
            predicted_step = predicted_steps[index]
            if expected_step == predicted_step:
                exact_steps += 1
            correct_fields += sum(
                expected_step.get(field) == predicted_step.get(field)
                for field in STEP_FIELDS
            )

    sample_count = len(case_ids)
    metrics: dict[str, object] = {
        "sample_cases": sample_count,
        "status_correct": status_matches,
        "status_accuracy": status_matches / sample_count,
        "exact_rows": row_matches,
        "row_accuracy": row_matches / sample_count,
        "exact_step_matches": exact_steps,
        "possible_aligned_steps": possible_steps,
        "step_accuracy": exact_steps / possible_steps if possible_steps else 1.0,
        "correct_step_fields": correct_fields,
        "possible_step_fields": possible_fields,
        "field_accuracy": correct_fields / possible_fields if possible_fields else 1.0,
        "exact_sequences": sequence_matches,
        "sequence_accuracy": sequence_matches / sample_count,
    }
    if include_details:
        metrics["mismatches"] = case_diagnostics
    return metrics


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset-dir",
        type=Path,
        default=CODE_DIR.parent / "dataset",
        help="Participant-facing dataset directory.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--details", action="store_true", help="Include case-level operation differences.")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(json.dumps(compare_samples(args.dataset_dir, include_details=args.details), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
    return 0
