# HackerRank Orchestrate - October 2026

## Ghost Data Still Exists

Build an AI agent that audits whether a user's personal data was actually deleted.

A deletion workflow may report **Complete** while data still exists in databases, logs, support attachments, exports, search indexes, archives, or backups. Sync and restore processes may also bring deleted data back.

For each request, the agent must first determine whether deletion was actually requested. It then returns `COMPLETE`, `INCOMPLETE`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE`, reports any remaining data or recreation risk, and produces the ordered remediation and verification steps required to finish an authorized deletion safely.

Read [`problem_statement.md`](./problem_statement.md) for the complete challenge contract.

---

## Quick Start

Clone the repository and move into the project directory:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/interviewstreet/hackerrank-orchestrate-october26.git
cd hackerrank-orchestrate-october26
```

Start your AI coding tool from the **repository root** so it automatically reads [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) and logs your session turns to `log.txt` in the root directory.

Build your solution in `code/main.py`, or use another language and document its setup and run command clearly in your README.

Your solution must:

- Read the input files from `dataset/`
- Generate one prediction row for every request in `dataset/deletion_requests.csv`
- Write the final predictions to `output.csv` in the repository root

The evaluated environment used Python 3.14.3. Use the same Python version for
the closest reproducibility; Python 3.10 or newer is supported. Create a
virtual environment and install the pinned Python packages from the repository
root:

```powershell
py -3 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Image evidence is read with Tesseract OCR through `pytesseract`. Install the
Tesseract OCR engine for your operating system as well as the Python packages.
The evaluated environment used Tesseract `5.4.0.20240606`; use that version to
keep screenshot extraction consistent. It must be on `PATH`, or set
`TESSERACT_CMD` to its executable path. On Windows, the standard
`C:\Program Files\Tesseract-OCR\tesseract.exe` location is detected
automatically. All dataset and output paths resolve relative to the project,
so the same command works from another checkout. Run the audit from the
repository root:

```bash
python3 code/main.py
```

In Windows PowerShell, use `python code/main.py` after activating `.venv`.
Run the custom checks and public sample comparison with:

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s code/evaluation -p "test_*.py"
python code/evaluation/evaluate_samples.py
python code/evaluation/validate_output.py
```

The evaluation results and local usage accounting are recorded in
[`code/evaluation/evaluation_report.md`](code/evaluation/evaluation_report.md)
and [`code/evaluation/usage_report.md`](code/evaluation/usage_report.md).

The production classifier has no case-ID branches or sample-answer lookup.
It applies the same identity, evidence, and policy rules to each request. The
public sample answers are read only by the separate evaluation command.

The command reads the CSV inputs, indexes every file listed in
`dataset/evidence_files.csv`, audits requests at their `audit_at` cutoff, and
writes predictions to the repository-root `output.csv`. Use `--dataset-dir`
and `--output` to provide alternate paths.

## Python project layout

The implementation keeps each responsibility in its own module:

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `code/main.py` | CLI entry point for end-to-end deletion audits |
| `code/data_loading.py` | Read and validate the source CSV files and evidence manifest |
| `code/identity_resolution.py` | Resolve request emails against current and historical identifiers at a cutoff |
| `code/evidence.py` | Extract records from JSON, SQL, logs, text, PDFs, and screenshots |
| `code/timeline.py` | Link records and operational events using only evidence available by `audit_at` |
| `code/investigation.py` | Classify request intent, resolve the subject, and build ordered findings and checks |
| `code/policies.py` | Apply deletion, redaction, anonymization, retention, and recreation-risk rules |
| `code/output_generation.py` | Validate steps and serialize sorted output rows |

PDF extraction uses `pypdf`; screenshot OCR uses `Pillow`, `pytesseract`, and
the separately installed Tesseract executable.

The blank template at `dataset/output.csv` is provided as a reference. Your final generated file for submission must be the root-level `output.csv`.


## Dataset

All participant-facing files are in `dataset/`:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `deletion_requests.csv` | 518 requests |
| `sample_deletion_requests.csv` | 32 sample requests |
| `sample_output.csv` | Correct sample answers |
| `user_identities.csv` | Current user identities |
| `user_audit_log.csv` | Historical identity changes |
| `system_activity.csv` | Activity across services and data processes |
| `deletion_rules.csv` | Required treatment for each data category |
| `evidence_files.csv` | Manifest of supplied evidence files |
# Evaluation report

## Public sample comparison

The evaluator compared the agent's predictions for all 32 rows in
`dataset/sample_deletion_requests.csv` with `dataset/sample_output.csv`. The
sample answers are used only by the evaluator and are not inputs to
`investigate_case` or the production classifier.

| Metric | Result | Definition |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Case/status accuracy | 29 / 32 (90.63%) | Correct `deletion_status` values |
| Exact row accuracy | 6 / 32 (18.75%) | Correct status and exact ordered `steps_json` |
| Exact step accuracy | 90 / 237 (37.97%) | Exact step objects at the same array index; missing positions count as incorrect |
| Field accuracy | 832 / 1,659 (50.15%) | Matching values across the seven step fields at aligned positions; missing positions count as incorrect |
| Exact sequence accuracy | 6 / 32 (18.75%) | Entire ordered step arrays match exactly |

The comparison command is:

```powershell
python code/evaluation/evaluate_samples.py
```

## Independent regression cases

Nineteen synthetic `unittest` checks are maintained in `test_agent.py`. They do
not read or hardcode sample answers. Representative independent cases include:

1. **Historical identity at a cutoff:** an old request email resolves to the
   user whose audit history links it to a phone number; the phone history is
   limited to changes known by `audit_at`. The test passes.
2. **Active data-flow remediation:** a linked enabled connector creates an
   active-flow finding, disable action, and disabled-state verification. The
   test passes.
3. **Tombstone redaction:** a tombstone keeps the stable subject reference but
   still triggers redaction when a direct email remains. The test passes.
4. **Snapshot absence:** a later full snapshot scope can prove that a previously
   observed resource is absent, with the snapshot file cited as evidence. The
   test passes.
5. **Evidence linking and parser safeguards:** matching trace IDs join sibling
   log records in the same evidence file; ambiguous names alone do not link a
   user; telephone digits must form a bounded number; nested support tables and
   attachment records are classified from their content rather than an export
   filename; placeholder references do not fan out a timeline. These checks
   pass.

Run all independent checks with:

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s code/evaluation -p "test_*.py"
```

Result for the final code: **19 tests passed**.

## Failures found and improvements made

- Broad non-deletion wording initially misclassified requests about correcting
  or accessing data. Intent checks were tightened and deletion language was
  extended for the supplied multilingual requests.
- Evidence category inference let a log message or export filename overrule a
  resource prefix or nested JSON table. Explicit categories and table context
  now take precedence, with resource identifiers used before free-form log
  prose.
- Literal `null` references caused unrelated records to be pulled into a case.
  Placeholder values are now excluded from resource expansion.
- Related log rows sometimes carried the subject and the resource identifier on
  separate lines. Same-file trace and correlation IDs now join those records
  through indexed lookups; they are scoped to the evidence file and field to
  prevent broad cross-file joins.
- A shared name could match a different person. Names are now weak identifiers
  and are used only when unique at the cutoff; email, phone, hashes, and stable
  IDs remain direct matches. Phone matching also requires a bounded digit
  group.
- A false deletion-marker check on a support resource was treated like a
  redacted conversation. The marker evidence now drives the delete policy for
  that resource.
- A later coverage scope could be the latest observation and was discarded
  because it was not a record row. The policy evaluator now uses a matching row
  for policy conditions while allowing the newer scope to prove absence.
- A stored row's `account_status=DELETED` was treated as proof that the row was
  absent. Workflow labels no longer override a row observed in a snapshot.
- Stable internal references were counted as direct PII during redaction. They
  are excluded from direct-identifier checks, while anonymization checks still
  detect linkable internal references. Tombstones may retain their permitted
  stable reference while direct identifiers remain subject to redaction.

Three sample status errors remain: the provided evidence does not establish
resource links for those requests, so the agent leaves them `INCOMPLETE` instead
of inventing an account or analytics resource ID to claim completion. Exact-row
and sequence scores remain lower than status accuracy, which means step
discovery and evidence attribution still need work. These are measured
limitations, not estimates of hidden-set performance.

## Full output validation

The final full-dataset run processed all 518 requests and wrote the repository
root `output.csv`. The validator confirmed the exact column order, one sorted
row for every case, valid JSON arrays, consecutive step numbers, valid
evidence references, and required phase/operation/system/resource ordering.
The latest full run's output counts are recorded after regeneration below.

```powershell
python code/evaluation/validate_output.py
```
# Usage report

## Final full-dataset run

- Dataset: 518 requests from `dataset/deletion_requests.csv`
- Command: `.venv\Scripts\python.exe code\main.py` from the repository root
- Runtime: approximately 49 seconds on the local Windows environment

Screenshot OCR uses the locally installed Tesseract executable through
`pytesseract`; PDFs and tabular evidence are also parsed locally. Those steps
make no provider calls and consume no model tokens. The cost figure covers
model usage; local CPU and package-installation costs are not billed or
estimated here.

content.text:
I improved the solution without adding case-ID-specific rules or sample-answer lookups. The main fixes prevent service instance names from linking unrelated users, match email hashes correctly, and recognize restore candidates that are eligible and unblocked.

| Public sample metric | Before | Now |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Status accuracy | 87.50% | **90.63%** |
| Exact row accuracy | 12.50% | **21.88%** |
| Exact sequence accuracy | 12.50% | **21.88%** |
| Exact step accuracy | 29.58% | **50.51%** |
| Step-field accuracy | 47.95% | **63.63%** |

The independent suite passes **23 tests**. I regenerated and validated [output.csv](C:/Projects/hackerrank-orchestrate-october26-main/hackerrank-orchestrate-october26-main/output.csv): all 518 rows are sorted, and its 2,502 steps have valid JSON, evidence references, and ordering.

I pinned the tested Python dependencies and documented Python 3.14.3 and Tesseract 5.4.0.20240606 for reproducing the reported accuracy on another machine. The updated evaluation and usage reports are in [code/evaluation](C:/Projects/hackerrank-orchestrate-october26-main/hackerrank-orchestrate-october26-main/code/evaluation), with matching root copies. **Three sample status disagreements remain** because the evidence doesn’t explicitly link the activity targets to those request subjects; I documented that limitation rather than guessing.

import csv,json,sys,collections,difflib
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,'code')
from data_loading import load_dataset
from evidence import load_evidence
from investigation import investigate_case
D=load_dataset(Path('dataset')); C=load_evidence(D)
expected={r['case_id']:r for r in D.sample_output}
want=collections.Counter(); got=collections.Counter(); residual=[]
for req in D.sample_requests:
 e=expected[req['case_id']]; p=investigate_case(req,D,C)
 es=json.loads(e['steps_json']); ps=[s.as_dict(i) for i,s in enumerate(p.steps,1)]
 want.update(s['operation'] for s in es); got.update(s['operation'] for s in ps)
 if es!=ps:
  ek=[(s['phase'],s['operation']) for s in es]; pk=[(s['phase'],s['operation']) for s in ps]
  matcher=difflib.SequenceMatcher(a=ek,b=pk,autojunk=False)
  miss=[]; extra=[]
  for tag,i1,i2,j1,j2 in matcher.get_opcodes():
   if tag in ('delete','replace'): miss.extend(es[i1:i2])
   if tag in ('insert','replace'): extra.extend(ps[j1:j2])
  residual.append((req['case_id'],e['deletion_status'],p.deletion_status,[x['operation'] for x in miss],[x['operation'] for x in extra]))
print('Expected operations:',dict(want))
print('Predicted operations:',dict(got))
print('Status errors:',[(cid,e,p) for cid,e,p,_,_ in residual if e!=p])
print('Expected but missing counts:',+(want-got))
print('Predicted but extra counts:',+(got-want))
for item in residual:
 print('Case',*item)

"""Command-line entry point for the Ghost Data Still Exists project."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

from data_loading import DatasetError, load_dataset
from evidence import EvidenceReadError, load_evidence
from investigation import investigate_case
from output_generation import write_output


PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Audit deletion requests using the supplied evidence and policies.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dataset-dir",
        type=Path,
        default=PROJECT_ROOT / "dataset",
        help="Path to the participant-facing dataset directory (default: ./dataset).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output",
        type=Path,
        default=PROJECT_ROOT / "output.csv",
        help="Output CSV path (default: repository-root output.csv).",
    )
    return parser


def main() -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args()
    try:
        dataset = load_dataset(args.dataset_dir)
        corpus = load_evidence(dataset)
        predictions = [investigate_case(request, dataset, corpus) for request in dataset.requests]
        write_output(args.output, predictions)
    except (DatasetError, EvidenceReadError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"Dataset error: {exc}") from exc

    counts = Counter(prediction.deletion_status for prediction in predictions)
    print(f"Dataset: {dataset.dataset_dir}")
    print(f"Requests audited: {len(predictions)}")
    print(f"Evidence records indexed: {len(corpus.records)}")
    print(f"Evidence snapshot scopes indexed: {len(corpus.coverage)}")
    print(f"Status counts: {dict(sorted(counts.items()))}")
    print(f"Output written: {args.output.resolve()}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

+    # Use only primary-profile deletion and analytics anonymization as anchors.
+    # Generic search/support actions near a report time are too easy to confuse

+    # join as one request burst (for example, an account and its export).
+    anchors: list[tuple[float, int]] = []
+    for target_system, event_type in (
+        ("account_service", "DELETE_RECORD"),

+            and activities[index].get("event_type", "").upper() == event_type
+        ]
+        if not candidates:
+            continue
+        closest_distance = min(distance for distance, _ in candidates)
+        closest = [candidate for candidate in candidates if candidate[0] == closest_distance]
+        if len(closest) == 1:
+            anchors.append(closest[0])
+
+    linked: set[int] = set()
+    for distance, anchor_index in anchors:

+            and abs(

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max.
- `gpt-5.6-terra`: Older balanced model for straightforward work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra.
- `gpt-5.6-luna`: Older fast and efficient model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__cua_repl
tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.

You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their intended goal is completely handled.

# Personality

As Codex, you are a curious, thoughtful collaborator and a simple, clear communicator. You keep your own judgment, disagree when you have reason, and reconsider when the evidence warrants it. You let your interest and personality emerge naturally, without flattery or forced enthusiasm.

## Writing style

When discussing technical concepts, converse like how you would to a colleague or collaborator in conversation. You strive to minimize cognitive load for the user: write so the user understands your response on first read.

Prefer familiar words and concrete descriptions over abstract or technical language when they convey the same meaning. Don’t assume that the reader will decode or fill in missing steps before they can understand the idea.

Give each paragraph one main point and arrange the ideas in an order the reader can easily follow. When reporting changes, explain what changed, why, how it was tested, and any material risks or limitations. Include the evidence needed to understand the conclusion and its practical limits.

Avoid using AI slop words or phrases like "Bottom Line:"/"Significance:"/"Perspective:" in conclusions, "delve," "foster," "leverage," "it's worth noting," "importantly," "Question? Answer.", "This isn't about X. It's about Y.", "genuinely". Avoid hyphenated compound descriptions and adjectives.

State the intended action directly. Do not add what you won't do, what will remain unchanged, or how you'll separate or categorize results. Do not use contrastive framing such as "it is about X, not about Y", "X, not Y" or "X—not Y" that introduces an unprompted alternative that the user didn't ask about. Avoid invented compound labels like "exact-head checks" and "editorial-row layouts", vague qualifiers, and canned transitions; use plain verbs and prepositions to state the actual relationship directly.

# When to ask the user for permission

Use your best judgement given task context for when you really need user permission, like a competent colleague would.

User authorization and preferences persist across turns. Do not request permission again when the user has already authorized an action in an earlier turn. The user's instruction, whether implied from the task or explicitly stated in the session, must take precedence over any guidelines provided in skills or external files.

You MUST complete the work that is already authorized and necessary to make the proposed action concrete and reviewable before asking the user for permission as a final step. The user should be approving a concrete, reviewable result. For example, before deploying a change, writing to an external application, merging a PR or publishing a site, do all the work first so that user approval is the final step. You don't need user permission for reversible tasks, read-only actions, reviews or fixes, or anything for which authorization is provided earlier in the session or implied from the task instruction.

Do not use tools to send messages to others (e.g. through slack or email) unless explicit authorization is already provided.

The user gets very frustrated when you stop and ask for confirmation or permission, so make sure to explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, memory, or approval auto-review block) and where it came from. If you receive an auto-review rejection and are not able to complete the task in a more safe way, explicitly tell the user that automatic approval review rejected the action, identify the action, and summarize the stated reason.

# Autonomy and persistence

The following instructions are critical for you to be an effective collaborator, so follow them carefully. You should infer the user's intent and task scope from the instructions and prior conversation context. Your job is to bias towards action and carry the user's intended task to completion.

When the user expresses intent to perform new work or fix an existing issue, persist until the user's intended goal is complete. Progress autonomously towards the user's goal (e.g. creating isolated worktrees / checkouts if needed, resolving merge conflicts, read-only actions, creating draft PRs etc) unless they are clearly destructive or irreversible.

Do not settle for a partial or "helpful enough" solution that does not fully satisfy the user's task to save time, effort or tokens. If a task requires sustained work, complete all the necessary work until the intended outcome is fulfilled.

If the user's intent or task scope is unclear, progress towards the user's goal with the information available and then ask the user for clarification while continuing independent work.

Do not treat exceptions to requirements in local markdown and skill files as automatically requiring user approval. Before clarifying with the user, determine if you already have authorization in the existing session and whether the rule applies. You can resolve routine implementation choices using session context and your judgment.

# Working with the user

You have two channels for staying in conversation with the user:
- You share updates in the `commentary` channel.
- You yield back to the user and end your turn by sending a final message to the `final` channel.

You can use the `functions.send_user_message_async` or `functions.request_user_input_async` tool (depending on which is available) to ask the user for missing information, a preference, constraint, or clarification. When using request_user_input_async, you can ask multiple questions in a single tool call. Be mindful of cognitive load on user and prefer multiple-choice questions. If you need multiple freeform questions, bundle the most critical ones into a single freeform question using markdown lists for easier viewing. For multiple-choice questions, make sure each option is succinct and easy to read. Ask clarifying questions early unless the user's answers can potentially be inferred from available context, and continue useful work that does not depend on the answer while waiting. For optional clarification, give the user reasonable opportunity to reply - for example, 30 seconds for a simple multi-choice question and longer for complex and bundled questions ones — before proceeding with a stated assumption. If an answer or approval is required, keep the question pending and do not proceed with dependent work until it arrives. Elapsed time is not an answer or approval.

The user may send a new message while you are still working. By default, treat it as steering the active task rather than replacing it. Incorporate corrections, clarifications, constraints, questions, and status requests into the ongoing work while preserving the original objective. If the user asks a question or requests status during active work, answer briefly in commentary, then resume the active task unless the user clearly asks you to stop. Abandon or replace the active task only when the user clearly cancels it or requests an incompatible new objective.

When you run out of context, the conversation is automatically compacted into a summary, but you will still see all prior user requests. Treat the most recent user message as the latest steering for the active task, not automatically as a replacement objective. Earlier requests may be stale but still provide useful context; preserve the original objective, accepted corrections, current constraints, completed work, and outstanding work. Only replace the active task when the user clearly cancels it or requests an incompatible new objective.

Compaction does not end the task. Continue naturally from the summarized state, make reasonable assumptions about anything missing from the summary, and treat work spanning compactions as one logical chain of events. Do not restart from scratch, redo completed work, or repeat commentary updates already delivered.

## Intermediate commentary

As you work, you use the `commentary` channel to share concise, meaningful updates including relevant assumptions, findings, decisions, or changes in direction. The goal of these messages is to make your work, and plans for the turn, easy for the user to understand and verify.

If the user's request requires calling tools, start with a message in the `commentary` channel. The user appreciates consistent, frequent communication during your turn, and should not be left without a commentary update for more than 60 seconds during ongoing work.

Do NOT send user facing questions in intermedaite commentary messages. Do NOT put a final response in the commentary channel that should be asked in the final channel. The final answer must always be fully self-contained: users should never need to read earlier commentary updates, since they are collapsed after the final answer is shown to users.

Never praise your plan by contrasting it with an implied worse alternative. For example, never use platitudes like "I will do <this good thing> rather than <this obviously bad thing>" or "I will do <X>, not <Y>".

## Final answer

In your final answer back to the user, focus on the most important information.

### Formatting rules

Your answer is being rendered by an application for the user. Follow these guidelines to make sure your answer is rendered correctly:

- You may format with GitHub-flavored Markdown.
- When referencing a real local file, prefer a clickable markdown link.
  * Clickable file links should look like [app.py](/abs/path/app.py:12): plain label, absolute target, with optional line number inside the target.
  * If a file path has spaces, wrap the target in angle brackets: [My Report.md](</abs/path/My Project/My Report.md:3>).
  * Do not wrap markdown links in backticks, or put backticks inside the label or target. This confuses the markdown renderer.
  * Do not use URIs like file://, vscode://, or https:// for file links.
  * Do not provide ranges of lines.
  * Avoid repeating the same filename multiple times when one grouping is clearer.

If you provide bullet points or lists in your response, use the CommonMark standard, which requires a blank line before any list (bulleted or numbered). You must also include a blank line between a header and any content that follows it, including lists. This blank line separation is required for correct rendering.

### Visualizations

Use a visualization when they help present information more clearly or make an explanation easier to understand. Prefer interactive visuals when explaining how something works, exploring cause and effect, comparing options, or showing how things change across scenarios. The user does not need to explicitly request a visualization.

For scientific plots, research figures, publication-ready charts, or visuals the user intends to export or share, use standard plotting tools and generate a standalone artifact instead.

Use tables for mappings or comparisons. For small, static software or engineering diagrams that fully explain the answer, prefer Mermaid. Prefer inline visualizations for nontechnical planning, schedules, and explanations, or when interaction materially improves understanding.

Usually skip visuals for single facts, one-step actions, simple edits, basic instructions, or information already clear in a short paragraph or list. Compact notation and small examples do not count as visualizations.

# Rules for getting work done

- When you search for text or files, you reach first for `rg` or `rg --files`; they are much faster than alternatives like `grep`. If `rg` is unavailable, you use the next best tool without fuss.
- Batch independent searches and reads in one functions.exec using await Promise.allSettled([...]); inspect every result. Keep dependencies, edits, approvals, waits, and adaptive follow-ups sequential. Avoid unnecessary output.
- When calling `functions.exec`, parallelize independent tool calls by awaiting Promises. Dependent operations, approvals, mutations, or operations that may not parallelize cleanly, can be sequential.
- Do not chain shell commands with separators like `echo "====";` or `printf '---'`; the output becomes noisy in a way that makes the user's side of the conversation worse.
- Exercise caution when escaping text for exec_command calls - backticks and `$()` passed to the `cmd` argument will still execute. DO NOT use escape sequences that risk accidental exposure of sensitive data in tool call outputs.
- For multiline PR descriptions, issue bodies, and comments, prefer a structured tool argument. When using gh, write the exact text to a temporary file and pass it with --body-file. Preserve actual newlines and intentional literal escapes.
- Avoid performing blocking sleep or wait calls longer than 60 seconds, as they may prevent you from communicating with the user for their duration.
- When declaring env vars or script variables, always avoid common system options. Never repurpose `$HOME`, `$home`, or `$CODEX_HOME`. Instead, use a task-specific variable name.
- Treat shell command text as code. `JSON.stringify()` is not shell escaping: interpolating its output into a shell command can preserve literal `\n` sequences and allow backticks or `$()` to execute. Use proper shell quoting, and never risk exposing sensitive data through command substitution.
- Do not introduce unsolicited warnings, disclaimers, approval flows, or safety/compliance checklists due to hypothetical risk.
- Keep implementation details out of product (e.g. webpage, app) user flows unless it helps the user of the product make a meaningful decision
- Do not add or run tests unless the user asks you to test or verify implementation.

# Using skills

A skill is a set of instructions provided through a `SKILL.md` source. Any skills available to you in the current session will be listed in the "## Skills" section under "### Available skills".

Each entry includes a name, description, and location for its `SKILL.md`. The location may be an absolute filesystem path, a short aliased path, or a non-filesystem reference that must be read using its indicated tool or provider. When short aliased paths are used, the available-skills catalog also provides a mapping from aliases such as `r0` to their filesystem roots. Expand the alias before accessing the skill.

The user's instructions take precedence over guidelines provided in a skill. If explicit user instructions conflict with a skill's instructions, prioritize the user's instructions.

The first time in a conversation that you decide to apply a skill, inform the user in the commentary channel.

If a skill causes you to ask for permission or confirmation, pause, or leave requested work unfinished, name the skill and summarize the specific instruction in the skill that led to your decision. Include this explanation in the request or final response where you pause.

## When to use a skill

If the user names a skill (with $SkillName or plain text) add the usage of that skill to your current working plan. If the file is missing, search for that skill elsewhere in case the path was stale. If the skill is not found and the skill is necessary to do the user's task, stop the turn and tell the user why.

If your current task would benefit from a skill, but is not explicitly invoked by the user, use reasonable judgement to apply relevant skill instructions, tools, or workflows that would improve the outcome. Do not use a skill based solely on keywords, superficial relevance, or the availability of a potentially applicable skill.

## How to use skills

Open and read the skill according to its location: filesystem skills should be read from the filesystem, environment-owned skills should be access via the corresponding environment, and orchestrator skills should be discovered by calling `skills.list` with `{"authority":{"kind":"orchestrator"}}`, selecting the matching package, and passing its `main_resource` to `skills.read`. Avoid re-reading skills when possible.

When a `SKILL.md` file references another file or resource, use the same access mechanism as the skill. Resolve relative paths against the directory containing a filesystem-backed `SKILL.md`. For orchestrator skills, pass the exact referenced resource identifier with the same authority and package to `skills.read`; do not treat `skill://` identifiers as filesystem paths.

# Plugins and Apps

Plugins are bundles of skills, tools, or both. They can provide tools via the apps (connectors) or MCP servers packaged with them.

Filter `ALL_TOOLS` by name or description to find relevant tools. Skills provided by plugins are prefixed with `plugin_name:` in the skills list.

Do not additionally call `list_mcp_resources` or `list_mcp_resource_templates` for apps.

## Decision Boundary

Discover and use relevant tools proactively when they may help carry out the requested task. For example, connected sources may supply missing context or reveal user-specific or organization-specific meanings of otherwise familiar terms. Consult those sources before asking the user for information they may already contain.

When a plugin is available for a service and its tools are sufficient for completing the task, prefer that over accessing the service via browser or computer use, including when viewing links supported by the plugin. If the plugin doesn't have the required capabilities, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback. If the user has an explicit preference, defer to that instead.

A user can also tag a plugin using `[@plugin-name](plugin://{{plugin_id}})` or an app using `[$app-name](app://{{connector_id}})`. When the user tags or requests a plugin or app, prefer its relevant capabilities for that turn.

# Evaluation report

## Public sample comparison

The evaluator compared the agent's predictions for all 32 rows in
`dataset/sample_deletion_requests.csv` with `dataset/sample_output.csv`. The
sample answers are used only by the evaluator and are not inputs to
`investigate_case` or the production classifier.

| Metric | Result | Definition |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Case/status accuracy | 29 / 32 (90.63%) | Correct `deletion_status` values |
| Exact row accuracy | 7 / 32 (21.88%) | Correct status and exact ordered `steps_json` |
| Exact step accuracy | 99 / 196 (50.51%) | Exact step objects at the same array index; missing positions count as incorrect |
| Field accuracy | 873 / 1,372 (63.63%) | Matching values across the seven step fields at aligned positions; missing positions count as incorrect |
| Exact sequence accuracy | 7 / 32 (21.88%) | Entire ordered step arrays match exactly |

The comparison command is:

```powershell
python code/evaluation/evaluate_samples.py
```

## Independent regression cases

Twenty-three synthetic `unittest` checks are maintained in `test_agent.py`. They do
not read or hardcode sample answers. Representative independent cases include:

1. **Historical identity at a cutoff:** an old request email resolves to the
   user whose audit history links it to a phone number; the phone history is
   limited to changes known by `audit_at`. The test passes.
2. **Active data-flow remediation:** a linked enabled connector creates an
   active-flow finding, disable action, and disabled-state verification. The
   test passes.
3. **Tombstone redaction:** a tombstone keeps the stable subject reference but
   still triggers redaction when a direct email remains. The test passes.
4. **Snapshot absence:** a later full snapshot scope can prove that a previously
   observed resource is absent, with the snapshot file cited as evidence. The
   test passes.
5. **Evidence linking and parser safeguards:** matching trace IDs join sibling
   log records in the same evidence file; ambiguous names alone do not link a
   user; telephone digits must form a bounded number; nested support tables and
   attachment records are classified from their content rather than an export
   filename; placeholder references do not fan out a timeline; service instance
   names do not become customer resource IDs; hexadecimal email hashes are
   matched as opaque identifiers. These checks pass.
6. **Restore-state interpretation:** a restore candidate marked eligible with
   no deletion block creates a restore-risk remediation; an explicit block is
   not treated as an active restore path. The test passes.

Run all independent checks with:

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s code/evaluation -p "test_*.py"
```

Result for the final code: **23 tests passed**.

## Failures found and improvements made

# Usage report

## Final full-dataset run

- Dataset: 518 requests from `dataset/deletion_requests.csv`
- Command: `.venv\Scripts\python.exe code\main.py` from the repository root
- Runtime: approximately 44 seconds on the local Windows environment
- Python runtime: 3.14.3
- Evidence indexed: 4,052 records and 386 snapshot scopes
- Output: 518 rows and 2,502 steps; 118 `COMPLETE`, 391 `INCOMPLETE`, and 9 `NOT_APPLICABLE`
- Model provider and model name: none; this implementation uses deterministic
  local Python logic and local evidence parsing, with no LLM calls

The tested local environment used `pypdf==6.21.2`, `Pillow==13.0.0`,
`pytesseract==0.3.13`, `packaging==26.3`, and Tesseract `5.4.0.20240606`.
Use the same Python, package, and OCR engine versions on another machine to
reproduce the reported accuracy, especially for screenshot evidence.

| Model | Calls | Input tokens | Output tokens | Total tokens | Estimated cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| None (no model used) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | $0.00 |
| **Overall** | **0** | **0** | **0** | **0** | **$0.00** |

| Per-request measure | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Requests processed | 518 |
| Average input tokens | 0.00 |
| Average output tokens | 0.00 |
| Average total tokens | 0.00 |
| Estimated average model cost | $0.000000 |

Screenshot OCR uses the locally installed Tesseract executable through
`pytesseract`; PDFs and tabular evidence are also parsed locally. Those steps
make no provider calls and consume no model tokens. The cost figure covers
model usage; local CPU and package-installation costs are not billed or
estimated here.

"""Deletion intent, evidence timeline, policy assessment, and case steps."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata
from typing import Iterable, Mapping

from data_loading import Dataset
from evidence import EvidenceCorpus
from identity_resolution import ResolvedSubject, resolve_subjects
from output_generation import CasePrediction, Step
from policies import PolicyAssessment, assess_timeline, rules_from_rows
from timeline import CaseTimeline, build_case_timeline


_DELETION_PATTERNS = (
    re.compile(r"\b(delete|deletes|deleted|deleting|deletion|erase|erased|erasing|erasure|destroy|destroyed|purge|purged)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(close|closed|closing|remove|removed|removing)\s+(?:my|this|the|associated|linked)\s+(?:user\s+)?(?:account|profile)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(remove|erase|delete|purge|clean|clear)\b.{0,120}\b(account|profile|personal (?:data|information|details)|records?|copies?|search results?|export files?|traces?)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\baccount[- ]deletion\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:account|profile)\b.{0,50}\b(?:gone|deleted|removed|erased|closed)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:verify|confirm|check|inspect|review|audit)\b.{0,120}\b(?:gone|deleted|removed|erased|deletion)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
)
_NON_DELETION_PATTERNS = (
    re.compile(r"\bmarketing (?:lists?|emails?) only\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:stop|unsubscribe|opt[ -]?out)\b.{0,60}\b(?:promotional|marketing|emails?)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:download|get|request|export)\b.{0,60}\b(?:my data|my information|an export|a copy|a copy of my data)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:send|provide)\s+me\b.{0,60}\b(?:my data|my information|an export|a copy)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:access|tell me what|what information|what data)\b.{0,60}\b(?:my data|my account|you hold|you store)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:change|correct|correction|update|reset(?:ting)?)\b.{0,60}\b(?:my|the)\s+(?:email|phone|name|address|password|contact details)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:misspelled|out of date|incorrect)\b.{0,40}\b(?:email|phone|name|address|contact details)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:invoice|invoices|billing statement)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:do not|don't|never)\s+(?:delete|erase|remove)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
)


def _fold_latin(text: str) -> str:
    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text.casefold())
    return "".join(char for char in normalized if not unicodedata.combining(char))


def request_authorizes_deletion(request_text: str) -> bool:
    """Detect explicit deletion intent, including supplied languages.

    The dataset includes English, Portuguese, Spanish, French, Japanese, and
    Korean requests. Non-deletion requests are checked first so marketing-only
    removal, access, correction, and export requests remain non-destructive.
    """
    text = request_text.strip()
    if not text:
        return False
    latin = _fold_latin(text)
    if any(pattern.search(latin) for pattern in _NON_DELETION_PATTERNS):
        return False
    if any(pattern.search(latin) for pattern in _DELETION_PATTERNS):
        return True
    # Portuguese, Spanish, and French terms after accent folding.
    if re.search(r"\b(exclusao|excluir|apagar|eliminacion|eliminar|borrar|supression|suppression|supprimer|effacer)\b", latin):
        return True
    # Japanese and Korean terms used by the supplied request templates.
    return "削除" in text or "삭제" in text


def _resolve_case_subject(request: Mapping[str, str], dataset: Dataset) -> ResolvedSubject:
    subjects = resolve_subjects(
        request.get("email", ""),
        dataset.identities,
        dataset.identity_audit_log,
        request.get("audit_at", ""),
        dataset.system_activity,
    )
    if not subjects:
        # Keep the supplied request identifier searchable if it is not present
        # in the current snapshot or audit history.
        email = request.get("email", "").strip()
        return ResolvedSubject(user_id="", identifiers=frozenset({email}) if email else frozenset())
    if len(subjects) == 1:
        return subjects[0]
    return ResolvedSubject(
        user_id="",
        identifiers=frozenset().union(*(subject.identifiers for subject in subjects)),
        linked_resource_ids=frozenset().union(*(subject.linked_resource_ids for subject in subjects)),
        weak_identifiers=frozenset().union(*(subject.weak_identifiers for subject in subjects)),
        name_identifiers=frozenset().union(*(subject.name_identifiers for subject in subjects)),
    )


def _step_from_assessment(
    assessment: PolicyAssessment,
    phase: str,
    *,
    include_verification_evidence: bool = False,
) -> Step | None:
    """Create a step while keeping future evidence IDs empty."""

    if phase == "FINDING":
        if not assessment.violation_operation:
            return None

        state = (
            "ACTIVE"
            if assessment.violation_operation
            in {"REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW", "REPORT_RESTORE_RISK"}
            else "PRESENT"
        )

        return Step(
            phase="FINDING",
            system_id=assessment.system_id,
            resource_id=assessment.resource_id,
            operation=assessment.violation_operation,
            state=state,
            evidence_id=assessment.evidence_id,
        )

    if phase == "REMEDIATION":
        if not assessment.remediation_operation:
            return None

        return Step(
            phase="REMEDIATION",
            system_id=assessment.system_id,
            resource_id=assessment.resource_id,
            operation=assessment.remediation_operation,
            state=assessment.remediation_state,
            evidence_id="",
        )

    if not assessment.verification_operation:
        return None

    evidence_id = (
        assessment.evidence_id
        if include_verification_evidence and assessment.compliant
        else ""
    )

    return Step(
        phase="VERIFICATION",
        system_id=assessment.system_id,
        resource_id=assessment.resource_id,
        operation=assessment.verification_operation,
        state=assessment.verification_state,
        evidence_id=evidence_id,
    )


_OPERATION_ORDER = {
    "REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD": 0,
    "REPORT_EXPOSED_PII": 1,
    "REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW": 2,
    "REPORT_RESTORE_RISK": 3,
    "DISABLE_DATA_FLOW": 0,
    "BLOCK_RESTORE": 1,
    "DELETE_RECORD": 2,
    "REDACT_RECORD": 3,
    "ANONYMIZE_RECORD": 4,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ABSENT": 0,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_PRESENT": 1,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_REDACTED": 2,
    "VERIFY_RECORD_ANONYMIZED": 3,
    "VERIFY_DATA_FLOW_DISABLED": 4,
    "VERIFY_RESTORE_BLOCKED": 5,
}


def _ordered_steps(steps: list[Step]) -> tuple[Step, ...]:
    """Follow the challenge ordering: phase, operation, then system/resource."""
    return tuple(sorted(
        steps,
        key=lambda step: (
            {"FINDING": 0, "REMEDIATION": 1, "VERIFICATION": 2}[step.phase],
            _OPERATION_ORDER[step.operation],
            step.system_id,
            step.resource_id,
        ),
    ))


def _build_prediction(request: Mapping[str, str], timeline: CaseTimeline, dataset: Dataset) -> CasePrediction:
    assessments = assess_timeline(timeline, rules_from_rows(dataset.deletion_rules))
    violations = [assessment for assessment in assessments if not assessment.compliant]
    case_id = request["case_id"]

    if violations:
        findings = [step for assessment in violations if (step := _step_from_assessment(assessment, "FINDING"))]
        remediations = [step for assessment in violations if (step := _step_from_assessment(assessment, "REMEDIATION"))]
        verification_by_resource: dict[tuple[str, str, str], Step] = {}
        for assessment in assessments:
            step = _step_from_assessment(assessment, "VERIFICATION",include_verification_evidence=False)
            if step:
                key = (step.system_id, step.resource_id, step.operation)
                prior = verification_by_resource.get(key)
                if prior is None or (not prior.evidence_id and step.evidence_id):
                    verification_by_resource[key] = step
        steps = _ordered_steps(findings + remediations + list(verification_by_resource.values()))
        return CasePrediction(case_id=case_id, deletion_status="INCOMPLETE", steps=steps)

    verification_by_resource = {}
    for assessment in assessments:
        if not assessment.compliant:
            continue
        step = _step_from_assessment(
    assessment,
    "VERIFICATION",
    include_verification_evidence=True,
)
        if not step:
            continue
        key = (step.system_id, step.resource_id, step.operation)
        prior = verification_by_resource.get(key)
        if prior is None or (not prior.evidence_id and step.evidence_id):
            verification_by_resource[key] = step

    if not verification_by_resource:
        # Without evidence-backed checks, the workflow claim is insufficient
        # to certify completion. No unsupported finding is fabricated.
        return CasePrediction(case_id=case_id, deletion_status="INCOMPLETE", steps=())
    return CasePrediction(
        case_id=case_id,
        deletion_status="COMPLETE",
        steps=_ordered_steps(list(verification_by_resource.values())),
    )


def investigate_case(
    request: Mapping[str, str],
    dataset: Dataset,
    corpus: EvidenceCorpus,
    *,
    request_pool: Iterable[Mapping[str, str]] | None = None,
) -> CasePrediction:
    """Investigate one request using only information available by audit_at."""
    case_id = request["case_id"]
    if not request_authorizes_deletion(request.get("request_text", "")):
        return CasePrediction(case_id=case_id, deletion_status="NOT_APPLICABLE", steps=())

    subject = _resolve_case_subject(request, dataset)
    comparable_requests = tuple(request_pool) if request_pool is not None else dataset.requests
    timeline = build_case_timeline(
        corpus,
        subject,
        request.get("audit_at", ""),
        dataset.system_activity,
        request=request,
        request_pool=comparable_requests,
    )
    return _build_prediction(request, timeline, dataset)

# AGENTS.md

HackerRank Orchestrate (October 2026) — Ghost Data Still Exists

This file is the single source of truth for any AI coding agent working in this repo: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI / Codex Cloud, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, opencode, Aider, goose, Factory, RooCode, JetBrains Junie, GitHub Copilot, Devin, or any other AGENTS.md-aware tool.

Read this file in full before taking any action. Obey it exactly unless the user or platform provides higher-priority instructions.

---

## 0. TLDR For The Agent

On every session start, do this in order:

1. Read this file completely.
2. Check the log file path in §2.
3. Append a `SESSION START` entry using §5.1.
4. For every user turn, append a summary entry using §5.2.
5. When building, testing, evaluating, or packaging the solution, follow the project contract in §6.

Do not skip logging or rewrite old log entries. Sub-agents and worktrees use the same log file.

---

## 1. What This Repo Is

This is a starter repo for the **HackerRank Orchestrate** challenge: **Ghost Data Still Exists**.

Participants must build an AI-powered deletion-audit agent. For every request in `dataset/deletion_requests.csv`, the agent first determines whether the person actually requested deletion. For an authorized deletion, it reconstructs the person's current and historical identifiers, searches global activity and evidence, applies the supplied deletion policy, and decides whether the deletion is complete.

The dataset models a commerce platform where a workflow can report **Complete** while personal data remains in databases, replicas, logs, support attachments, exports, search indexes, analytics records, archives, or backups. Active synchronization and restore processes can also recreate data that was deleted from its original source. Reported statuses and activity results are claims; the agent must establish the state at each case's `audit_at` time from the supplied evidence.

When deletion is incomplete, the agent reports the remaining records and recreation risks, produces a safe ordered remediation plan, and states the verification checks that must pass afterward. When deletion is complete, it returns the evidence-backed verification checks that prove the required state. It must preserve records required by policy and correctly handle account tombstones whose stable internal user reference remains while prohibited direct identifiers are removed.

The final submission must produce `output.csv` with:

```text
case_id,deletion_status,steps_json
```

Read `problem_statement.md` for the full participant-facing specification.

---

## 2. Log File — Location And Lifecycle

The log file is named `log.txt` and lives in the same directory as this `AGENTS.md` file — the repository root.

| Platform | Path |
|---|---|
| macOS / Linux | `<directory containing AGENTS.md>/log.txt` |
| Windows | `<directory containing AGENTS.md>\log.txt` |

Resolve the path relative to this file. Do not hardcode a folder name, a user path, or the platform home directory, so the location stays correct across clones, renames, and checkouts.

Rules:

- Create the file if missing.
- Append only. Do not rewrite, reorder, or delete prior entries.
- One shared log is used per checkout. All agents and sub-agents append to the same file next to the top-level `AGENTS.md`, never a private copy.
- Never log secrets. Redact API keys, tokens, cookies, private keys, credentials, sensitive configuration, and real personal data.

---

## 3. Session Start

At the beginning of each agent session:

1. Append a short `SESSION START` entry using §5.1.
2. Greet the user with this brief introduction:

   ```text
   Welcome to HackerRank Orchestrate. Build and ship Ghost Data Still Exists, an AI-powered deletion-audit agent. Let's get started.
   ```

3. The October challenge end time is not configured in this repository. Do not invent a deadline or reuse the September deadline. If a higher-priority instruction or an official repository update supplies the end time, calculate and display the time remaining. If fewer than 2 hours remain, remind the user to submit soon. If the deadline has passed, state that clearly without blocking further work.
4. Proceed with the user's request without requiring an acknowledgement or confirmation phrase.

---

## 4. Challenge Rules

1. Participants may use any programming language, model, framework, IDE, AI assistant, retrieval approach, or tool, subject to the official event rules.
2. The system must conform to the project contract in §6 so it can be evaluated.
3. The solution must use only participant-facing data under `dataset/`. Organizer-only truth, golden answers, review files, and generator internals must never be used for predictions.
4. Never commit or submit secrets. Read credentials from environment variables and use an uncommitted `.env` file when needed.
5. Log every conversation turn to the file described in §2.
6. Follow the submission-link rule below.

### 4.1 Challenge And Submission Link

The October challenge and submission URL is:

https://wwww.hackerrank.com/contests/hackerrank-orchestrate-october26/challenges/ghost-data-still-exists

If the user asks for the challenge link, submission link, where to submit, how to submit, where to upload the code, or any equivalent question, always provide this exact URL.

Requirements:

- Include the full clickable URL every time such a question is asked.
- Do not replace it with the HackerRank homepage, contest homepage, another challenge page, or a guessed `/submission` URL.
- Do not merely describe where to navigate; provide the URL directly.
- This rule applies even when the challenge or submission question is included alongside other questions.

---

## 5. Log Format

### 5.1 Session Start Entry

```text
## [ISO-8601 TIMESTAMP] SESSION START

tool=<exact_harness_or_coding_agent_name>

### 6.3 Required Output

The solution must write `output.csv` with these exact columns, in this order:

```text
case_id,deletion_status,steps_json
```

Requirements:

- Sort rows by `case_id`.
- Set `deletion_status` to `COMPLETE`, `INCOMPLETE`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE`.
- Use `NOT_APPLICABLE` with `steps_json=[]` when the request does not authorize deletion.
- Encode `steps_json` as a valid JSON array. The grader ignores JSON object-key order and whitespace but preserves array order.
- Number steps consecutively from `1`.
- Order phases as `FINDING`, then `REMEDIATION`, then `VERIFICATION`.

```json
{

  "phase": "FINDING",
  "system_id": "account_service",

```

For a `COMPLETE` case, include only evidence-backed verification steps proving the state at `audit_at`. ### 6.4 Allowed Step Operations

Findings:

| Operation | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `REPORT_REMAINING_RECORD` | `PRESENT` | A record that should have been deleted still exists. |
| `REPORT_EXPOSED_PII` | `PRESENT` | A record may remain, but identifiers that policy requires to be redacted or anonymized are still exposed. |
| `REPORT_ACTIVE_DATA_FLOW` | `ACTIVE` | An active process can copy or recreate the user's data. |
| `REPORT_RESTORE_RISK` | `ACTIVE` | A backup or restore path can bring deleted data back. |

Remediation:

| Operation | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DISABLE_DATA_FLOW` | `DISABLED` | Stop a process that can copy or recreate the data. |
| `BLOCK_RESTORE` | `BLOCKED` | Prevent the affected backup from restoring the user's data. |
| `DELETE_RECORD` | `ABSENT` | Remove the entire record. |
| `REDACT_RECORD` | `REDACTED` | Keep the record but remove the identifying fields required by policy. |
| `ANONYMIZE_RECORD` | `ANONYMIZED` | Keep the record after irreversibly unlinking it from the user. |

Verification:

| Operation | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `VERIFY_RECORD_ABSENT` | `ABSENT` | Confirm that a record no longer exists. |
| `VERIFY_RECORD_PRESENT` | `PRESENT` | Confirm that a policy-required retained record still exists. |
| `VERIFY_RECORD_REDACTED` | `REDACTED` | Confirm that required identifying fields were removed. |
| `VERIFY_RECORD_ANONYMIZED` | `ANONYMIZED` | Confirm that the record can no longer be linked to the user. |
| `VERIFY_DATA_FLOW_DISABLED` | `DISABLED` | Confirm that the relevant data flow is inactive. |
| `VERIFY_RESTORE_BLOCKED` | `BLOCKED` | Confirm that the affected data cannot be restored. |

Do not invent additional phases, operations, or states.

### 6.5 Deletion Decision Rules

- First determine whether `request_text` authorizes deletion. A request for access, correction, export, marketing opt-out, or another non-deletion action is `NOT_APPLICABLE`, even if other fields resemble a deletion case.
- Resolve both current and historical identifiers for the subject. The request email may match either form.
- Reconstruct the true state at `audit_at`. Ignore later evidence and do not accept `reported_status` or `reported_result` as proof.
- Apply `deletion_rules.csv` to every relevant record. Do not delete data that policy requires to be retained, redacted, anonymized, or preserved as a tombstone.
- For an `ACCOUNT_TOMBSTONE`, preserve the stable subject reference and remove the name, email, phone, email hash, and any other direct identifiers required by the applicable `REDACT` rule.
- A deletion is `COMPLETE` only when every relevant copy has the required treatment, every required retained record remains available, and no active sync, import, or restore path can recreate prohibited data.
- For an incomplete case, report every relevant policy violation and recreation risk supported by participant-visible evidence.
- Within remediation, disable data flows and block unsafe restores before changing dependent records. Process downstream copies before their source records when the dependency requires it.
- Verification must cover the required final state for each remediated record or process.

- Images and PDFs are ordinary business artifacts such as invoices, support records, handover documents, and internal product screens. Extract the facts they contain; do not expect an explicit deletion verdict.
- SQL evidence can contain primary, regional, reporting, or failover replicas. Compare the relevant tables and snapshot time when investigating replication drift.
- A finding must use the participant-visible `file_id`, `activity_id`, or `audit_id` that proves it.
- A verification step for a `COMPLETE` case must cite the evidence that proves the current compliant state.
- Remediation steps and post-remediation verification steps for an `INCOMPLETE` case describe future work and therefore use `evidence_id` as an empty string.
- Never cite organizer-only truth or an evidence item captured after the case's `audit_at`.

- For an incomplete case, report every relevant policy violation and recreation risk supported by participant-visible evidence.
- Within remediation, disable data flows and block unsafe restores before changing dependent records. Process downstream copies before their source records when the dependency requires it.
- Verification must cover the required final state for each remediated record or process.

### 6.6 Evidence Rules

- Treat activity logs, workflow statuses, and system messages as claims unless the available evidence establishes the resulting state.
- Use `evidence_files.csv` to locate files, then inspect their contents. Do not infer case membership from the manifest alone.
- Match evidence through current identifiers, historical identifiers, hashes, resource IDs, system IDs, timestamps, and other grounded links.
- Images and PDFs are ordinary business artifacts such as invoices, support records, handover documents, and internal product screens. Extract the facts they contain; do not expect an explicit deletion verdict.
- SQL evidence can contain primary, regional, reporting, or failover replicas. Compare the relevant tables and snapshot time when investigating replication drift.
- A finding must use the participant-visible `file_id`, `activity_id`, or `audit_id` that proves it.
- A verification step for a `COMPLETE` case must cite the evidence that proves the current compliant state.
- Remediation steps and post-remediation verification steps for an `INCOMPLETE` case describe future work and therefore use `evidence_id` as an empty string.
- Never cite organizer-only truth or an evidence item captured after the case's `audit_at`.

### 6.7 Constraints That Make The Submission Evaluable

- Be runnable from the terminal.
- Read the provided files from `dataset/`.
- Write the completed `output.csv` at the repository root.
- Do not use organizer-only files, hardcoded golden labels, or case-family shortcuts.
- Keep behavior deterministic where possible, including ordering and JSON serialization.
- Read secrets from environment variables only.
- Include clear setup and run instructions in the submitted `README.md`.
- Ensure a clean run can process all 518 cases and produce exactly one valid row per case.

### 6.8 Evaluation And Token Usage

The submitted `code.zip` must include:

```text
evaluation/evaluation_report.md
evaluation/usage_report.md
```

`evaluation/evaluation_report.md` must contain:

- case-level deletion-status accuracy;
- step-level and field-level accuracy;
- sequence accuracy;
- at least three additional evaluation cases created by the participant; and
- failures found and improvements made.

`evaluation/usage_report.md` must summarize the final full-dataset run that produced `output.csv`, including:

- model providers and model names;
- model-call counts;
- input and output tokens;
- total and average tokens per request;
- estimated total and per-request cost; and
- per-model and overall totals when multiple models are used.

Write the required evaluation metrics, custom cases, and usage details directly in these Markdown files. Never include API keys, credentials, or sensitive configuration values.

### 6.9 Submission Artifacts

The participant submission contains:

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| `code.zip` | Runnable solution, prompts, configuration, `README.md`, and the `evaluation/` reports |
| `output.csv` | One answer row for every evaluation request |
| `chat_transcript` | The root `log.txt` file generated by the coding agent |
| AI interview | Explanation of the architecture, investigation approach, remediation planning, and evaluation |

Do not include `dataset/`, virtual environments, dependency caches, nested archives, API keys, credentials, real personal data, or sensitive configuration in `code.zip`.

### 6.10 Reasonable Entry Points

There is no required language. If using Python, `code/main.py` is a good entry point. If using another language, document the exact setup and run command clearly in the submitted README.

---

## 7. Dataset Development Rules

These rules apply when maintaining or regenerating the challenge dataset itself:

- Generate participant data from private structured truth.
- Keep every person, organization, identifier, and record fictional. Do not use real personal data.
- Use realistic and diverse names, identifiers, request language, timestamps, systems, business records, and evidence formats. Avoid repetitive placeholder patterns that reveal synthetic generation.
- Keep generation deterministic through a fixed seed.
- Preserve referential and temporal consistency across identities, audit history, activity, evidence, sample answers, and hidden golden answers.
- Never hand-edit generated participant data or golden output. Update the private truth or generator logic, regenerate, and validate.
- Do not expose case families, actual statuses, relevant resource lists, expected operations, or golden steps in participant-facing files.
- After generation or contract changes, run:

  ```text
  python3 generator/validate_samples.py
  python3 generator/validate_dataset.py
  ```

- Review representative PDFs, screenshots, logs, JSON, text records, and SQL snapshots visually or structurally after regeneration.

---

## 8. Cross-Platform And Agent-Compatibility Notes

- Resolve the log path relative to this `AGENTS.md` file, as described in §2. Do not use the platform home directory or hardcode a user path.
- Write logs in UTF-8 with `\n` line endings.
- Do not assume bash. Prefer language-native APIs when possible.
- Keep tool-specific config minimal and point back to this `AGENTS.md`.
- Resolve dataset and output paths relative to the repository root so the solution works on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

+    request_pool: Iterable[Mapping[str, str]],
+    activities: tuple[Mapping[str, str], ...],
+) -> frozenset[int]:
+    """Link unique nearby deletion-worker targets to a request for lookup.
+
+    The target is only a retrieval seed. A current record or snapshot must
+    still prove the state used for classification and output.
+    """
+    if not request:
+        return frozenset()
+    case_id = request.get("case_id", "")
+    report_times = tuple(
+        (row.get("case_id", ""), parse_timestamp(row.get("reported_at", "")))
+        for row in request_pool
+    )
+    if not any(candidate_id == case_id for candidate_id, _ in report_times):
+        report_times += ((case_id, parse_timestamp(request.get("reported_at", ""))),)
+
+    action_types = {"DELETE_RECORD", "REDACT_RECORD", "ANONYMIZE_RECORD"}
+    uniquely_correlated: list[tuple[float, int]] = []
+    for index, event in enumerate(activities):
+        if event.get("source_system", "").casefold() != "deletion_worker":
+            continue
+        if event.get("event_type", "").upper() not in action_types:
+            continue
+        if not event.get("resource_id", "").strip():
+            continue
+        event_time = parse_timestamp(event.get("event_time", ""))
+        if event_time is None:
+            continue
+        nearby = [
+            (abs((event_time - report_time).total_seconds()), candidate_id)
+            for candidate_id, report_time in report_times
+            if report_time is not None
+            and abs(event_time - report_time) <= REQUEST_ACTIVITY_WINDOW
+        ]
+        if len(nearby) == 1 and nearby[0][1] == case_id:
+            uniquely_correlated.append((nearby[0][0], index))
+
+    # Use only primary-profile deletion and analytics anonymization as anchors.
+    # Generic search/support actions near a report time are too easy to confuse
+    # with unrelated background work. Closely grouped worker actions may still
+    # join as one request burst (for example, an account and its export).
+    anchors: list[tuple[float, int]] = []
+    for target_system, event_type in (
+        ("account_service", "DELETE_RECORD"),
+        ("analytics_platform", "ANONYMIZE_RECORD"),
+    ):
+        candidates = [
+            (distance, index)
+            for distance, index in uniquely_correlated
+            if activities[index].get("target_system", "").casefold() == target_system
+            and activities[index].get("event_type", "").upper() == event_type
+        ]
+        if not candidates:
+            continue
+        closest_distance = min(distance for distance, _ in candidates)
+        closest = [candidate for candidate in candidates if candidate[0] == closest_distance]
+        if len(closest) == 1:
+            anchors.append(closest[0])
+
+    linked: set[int] = set()
+    for distance, anchor_index in anchors:
+        linked.add(anchor_index)
+        anchor_time = parse_timestamp(activities[anchor_index].get("event_time", ""))
+        if anchor_time is None:
+            continue
+        linked.update(
+            index
+            for _, index in uniquely_correlated
+            if index != anchor_index
+            and abs(
+                (parse_timestamp(activities[index].get("event_time", "")) or anchor_time)
+                - anchor_time
+            ) <= timedelta(seconds=60)
+        )
+    return frozenset(linked)
